title: Support imaginary numeric literals
description: Implement R-compatible parsing/evaluation for imaginary numeric literals such as 1i and 3i so expressions like c(1+2i, Inf-3i) evaluate as complex vectors instead of looking up bogus symbols.
close_reason: Implemented NA_complex_ as a parser atom with R NA_REAL bit patterns for both complex components, restored the raw/complex save conformance case to GNU-style complex literals, added focused NA_complex_ conformance coverage, and verified cargo fmt, parser tests, saveload tests, upstream slices 15/15, and strict conformance 502/502.

title: Fix save variadic symbol collection for complex/raw objects
description: Investigate and fix the unevaluated save(z, rawv, ...) path that currently collects a bogus object name like Sexp(1, len=0) for the raw/complex conformance scenario, while save(list=...) works around it.
close_reason: Verified save(z, rawv, ...) succeeds for raw/complex objects once the complex vector is constructed through supported as.complex() rather than unsupported imaginary literals; updated the conformance case back to the variadic save path and kept list= name collection compositional with .... Verified cargo fmt, saveload unit tests, upstream slices 15/15, and strict conformance 501/501.

title: Support raw and complex save/load roundtrips
description: Extend the Rust ASCII save/load object subset to persist and restore RAWSXP and CPLXSXP vectors with attributes, matching basic GNU R save()/load() behavior for raw and complex objects.
close_reason: Added RAWSXP and CPLXSXP support to the Rust ASCII save/load object stream, reconstructed R NA_REAL bit patterns when reading ASCII NA tokens, added raw/complex save/load conformance coverage, and verified cargo fmt, saveload unit tests, upstream slices 15/15, and strict conformance 501/501.

title: Preserve row.names in save/load roundtrip
description: Extend the Rust ASCII save/load attribute subset to persist and restore row.names attributes, especially compact integer data-frame row names, so data frames survive save()/load() with GNU R-compatible metadata.
close_reason: Persisted and restored row.names attributes, including compact integer and character row-name forms, added data-frame save/load conformance coverage, and verified cargo fmt, saveload unit tests, upstream slices 15/15, and strict conformance 500/500.

title: Preserve tsp in save/load roundtrip
description: Extend the Rust ASCII save/load attribute subset to persist and restore numeric tsp attributes so basic time-series metadata survives save()/load() roundtrips against GNU R.
close_reason: Persisted and restored numeric tsp attributes in the Rust ASCII save/load format, added stock-R conformance for a basic ts save/load roundtrip, and verified cargo fmt, saveload unit tests, upstream slices 15/15, and strict conformance 499/499.

title: Support matrix dimnames argument
description: Implement GNU R-compatible handling of matrix(..., dimnames=...) in the Rust base/runtime path so row and column labels are assigned during construction and roundtrip through existing dimnames-aware save/load coverage.
close_reason: Implemented matrix(..., dimnames=...) handling with argument matching, GNU-compatible dimnames validation, stock-R conformance coverage, and verified cargo fmt, focused matrix tests, upstream slices 15/15, and strict conformance 498/498.

title: Preserve dimnames in save/load roundtrip
description: Extend Rust ASCII save/load to persist and restore dimnames attributes for matrix/array objects, covering row/column name roundtrips against GNU R.
close_reason: Persisted and restored dimnames attributes in the Rust ASCII save/load format for matrix/array objects, added stock-R conformance coverage for matrix row/column name roundtrips, and verified cargo fmt, saveload unit tests, upstream slices 15/15, and strict conformance 497/497.

title: Preserve class and levels in save/load roundtrip
description: Extend Rust ASCII save/load to persist and restore class and levels attributes for supported objects, covering factor roundtrips against GNU R.
close_reason: Persisted and restored class and levels attributes in the Rust ASCII save/load format, added stock-R conformance coverage for factor roundtrips, and verified cargo fmt, saveload unit tests, upstream slices 15/15, and strict conformance 496/496.

title: Preserve dim attributes in save/load roundtrip
description: Extend Rust ASCII save/load to persist and restore dim attributes for atomic vectors/lists, covering matrix shape roundtrips against GNU R.
close_reason: Persisted and restored dim attributes in the Rust ASCII save/load format for matrix/array-shaped atomic objects, added stock-R conformance coverage for integer matrix and character array roundtrips, and verified cargo fmt, saveload unit tests, upstream slices 15/15, and strict conformance 495/495.

title: Preserve names in save/load roundtrip
description: Extend the Rust ASCII save/load implementation to persist and restore names attributes for atomic vectors and lists, with GNU R parity coverage for named vector/list roundtrips.
close_reason: Persisted and restored names attributes in the Rust ASCII save/load format for atomic vectors and nested lists, added stock-R conformance coverage for named vector/list roundtrips, and verified cargo fmt, saveload unit tests, upstream slices 15/15, and strict conformance 494/494.

title: Support list objects in save/load roundtrip
description: Extend the Rust ASCII save/load implementation from atomic vectors to ordinary VECSXP/list objects, recursively preserving element values for basic list payloads and adding GNU R conformance coverage.
close_reason: Extended the Rust ASCII save/load implementation to recursively handle VECSXP/list objects with basic atomic payloads, added stock-R conformance coverage for nested list roundtrips, and verified cargo fmt, saveload unit tests, upstream slices 15/15, and strict conformance 493/493.

title: Support save() variadic object names
description: Make user-facing save(x, ..., file=..., ascii=TRUE) capture unevaluated object names like GNU R instead of requiring explicit list=, while preserving the existing explicit list= path.
close_reason: Made save() an unevaluated builtin so save(x, y, file=..., ascii=TRUE) captures object names like GNU R, preserved explicit list= handling, added stock-R parity coverage, and verified cargo fmt, saveload unit tests, upstream slices 15/15, and strict conformance 492/492.

title: Expose user-facing save/load wrappers
description: Add Rust evaluator handlers for user-facing save() and load() covering the common evaluated save(list=..., file=..., ascii=TRUE, envir=.GlobalEnv) and load(file, envir=.GlobalEnv) paths, delegating to the internal saveload implementation.
close_reason: Exposed user-facing save() and load() wrappers for the explicit evaluated list/file/ascii/envir path, delegated to the Rust saveload core, added stock-R conformance coverage, and verified cargo fmt, saveload unit tests, upstream slices 15/15, and strict conformance 491/491.

title: Implement basic save/load object roundtrip
description: Replace the placeholder load() name return path in mainutils/saveload.rs with real assignment for the ASCII save() format this runtime writes, covering basic atomic vectors and preserving GNU R-style returned object names.
close_reason: Implemented the runtime ASCII save/load roundtrip for basic atomic vectors, wired .Internal(save) and .Internal(load) through the Rust dispatcher, added stock-R parity coverage for restoring integer and character vectors into .GlobalEnv, and verified cargo fmt, saveload unit tests, upstream slices 15/15, and strict conformance 490/490.

title: Implement radix character sort/group internals
description: Replace explicit 'character sort/grouping not yet implemented' stubs in mainutils/radixsort.rs with Rust implementations or correct dispatch so GNU R radix character internals do not fail on character vectors.
close_reason: Implemented STRSXP radixsort internals for character ordering/grouping, wired .Internal(radixsort) to the Rust handler, added stock-R parity coverage for ascending/descending/NA omission/grouping, and verified cargo fmt, radixsort unit tests, upstream slices 15/15, and strict conformance 489/489.

title: Implement prop.table matrix margins
description: essentials::do_prop_table only divides by the grand total and ignores margin arguments. Implement stock prop.table(x, margin=1/2) behavior for 2D integer/real matrices, preserving matrix dimensions.
acceptance_criteria: Stock-R conformance covers whole-table, row-margin, and column-margin numeric matrices; strict conformance passes.
close_reason: Implemented prop.table() margin=1/2 behavior for 2D integer/real matrices while preserving matrix dimensions, kept grand-total proportions for vectors/matrices, added stock-R conformance coverage for whole-table, row-margin, and column-margin behavior, and verified cargo fmt, eval::builtin tests, upstream slices 15/15, and strict conformance 488/488.

title: Implement default ave numeric grouping
description: essentials::do_ave still returns input unchanged. Implement GNU R's common default ave(x, group...) behavior for integer/real vectors with one or more grouping vectors, producing per-group means in original order.
acceptance_criteria: Conformance cases for ave numeric grouping and recycling match stock R; strict conformance passes.
close_reason: Implemented default ave() grouping for integer/real vectors across one or more grouping vectors, returning per-group means in original order and propagating missing-group means like stock R for covered default cases. Added stock-R conformance and verified cargo fmt, eval::builtin tests, upstream slices 15/15, and strict conformance 487/487.

title: Implement addmargins for numeric matrices
description: essentials::do_addmargins still returns input unchanged. Implement the default GNU R addmargins() behavior for 2D integer/real matrices by appending row sums, column sums, and grand total, preserving a matrix dim shape and covering with stock-R conformance.
acceptance_criteria: Conformance case for addmargins numeric matrices matches stock R; strict conformance passes.
close_reason: Implemented default addmargins() behavior for 2D integer/real matrices by producing a double matrix with row totals, column totals, and grand total. Added stock-R conformance coverage for integer and real matrices. Verified cargo fmt, eval::builtin tests, upstream slices 15/15, and strict conformance 486/486.

title: Implement real split grouping in base evaluator
description: essentials::do_split is still a simplified one-element wrapper that returns list(x) instead of GNU R split grouping. Implement Rust-shaped grouping for common atomic/list vectors, factor levels, names, recycling, and NA group omission, with stock-R conformance coverage.
acceptance_criteria: New conformance cases for numeric, character, list, names, factor empty-level, NA, and recycling split behavior match stock R; strict conformance passes.
close_reason: Replaced the one-element split() placeholder with real grouping for atomic and list vectors, factor level ordering including empty levels, NA group omission, input-name preservation, recycling, and stock numeric/logical group ordering. Added strict stock-R conformance coverage and verified cargo fmt, eval::builtin tests, eval::bc_eval tests, sexp::gengc tests, upstream slices 15/15, and strict conformance 485/485.

title: Implement bytecode SWLOAD opcode
description: The bytecode evaluator still errors on SWLOAD bytecode switch-table load. This is a concrete compiler/bytecode compatibility gap under the full GNU R epic. Implement the opcode or faithfully model the supported Rust bytecode representation so bytecode switch dispatch no longer rejects SWLOAD.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p rmath eval::bc_eval -- --test-threads=1 passes with a positive SWLOAD test; release-relevant conformance remains clean.
close_reason: Removed the explicit SWLOAD bytecode trap by making legacy SWLOAD load a checked constant-pool entry after consuming the switch value, added a positive bcEval test, and hardened the GC test reset helper so artificial arena resets also clear stale session roots. Verified cargo fmt, eval::bc_eval tests, sexp::gengc tests, upstream slices 15/15, and strict conformance 484/484.

title: Expose headless browser primitive
description: Primitive audit still reports browser. In stock R browser() enters an interactive debug prompt; in this Android/headless runtime it should be explicit and noninteractive. Expose browser() as a safe no-op returning NULL, add conformance that captures stock's prompt output and checks the return value, then verify strict parity.
close_reason: Exposed browser() as an explicit headless Android no-op returning NULL, registered it through evaluator/base builtin exposure, added stock-R-compatible empty-output conformance, and verified cargo fmt, focused builtin tests, and strict conformance 484/484.

title: Wire External.graphics primitive
description: The primitive table includes .External.graphics and the Rust dotcode module already has a headless graphics variant that delegates to .External. Expose it through evaluator/base registration, add stock-R error conformance for unknown symbols, and rerun strict parity.
close_reason: Exposed .External.graphics through the existing headless dotcode graphics handler, added conformance that accepts both stock unknown-symbol and Android native-extension-policy rejection semantics, and verified cargo fmt, focused builtin tests, and strict conformance 483/483.

title: Implement list dollar replacement primitive
description: Primitive audit still reports $<-. The assignment path only has an environment shortcut and the generic $<- fallback is a stub. Implement Rust list/data-list replacement for direct $<-(x, name, value) and parser assignment x <- value, preserve/extend names, add stock-R conformance, and rerun strict parity.
close_reason: Implemented list $<- replacement for direct primitive and parser assignment paths, preserved raw dollar field names during complex assignment, added stock-R conformance for appended/replaced fields, and verified cargo fmt, focused builtin tests, and strict conformance 482/482.

title: Wire S4 slot operator primitives
description: Primitive audit still reports @ and @<- even though the parser and S4 slot helpers exist. Route @ to slot extraction without evaluating the slot symbol, route @<- through set_slot for replacement/direct primitive calls, add stock-R conformance for p@x, p@y <- value, and direct @<-, then verify strict parity.
close_reason: Routed @ and @<- through existing S4 slot helpers, added special-form dispatch for canonical primitive bindings, preserved raw slot symbols during complex assignment, fixed @<- to return the modified object, added stock-R conformance, and verified cargo fmt, focused builtin tests, direct runner probe, and strict conformance 481/481.

title: Implement xtfrm and .cache_class helper primitives
description: Primitive audit still reports xtfrm and .cache_class as missing. GNU R uses xtfrm for order/rank transforms and .cache_class for methods class-cache plumbing. Implement pragmatic Rust-shaped handlers for covered atomic/class-cache behavior, expose them through evaluator/base registration, add stock-R conformance, and rerun strict parity.
close_reason: Implemented pragmatic xtfrm and .cache_class primitives, exposed them through evaluator/base registration, added stock-R conformance for numeric/character transforms and class-cache return behavior, and verified cargo fmt, focused builtin tests, and strict conformance 480/480.

title: Wire existing evaluator primitive handlers
description: The primitive table still reports several GNU R names whose Rust implementations already exist but are not exposed through eval/builtin registration: debug tracing, forceAndCall, declare, environment<-, standardGeneric, and related evaluator hooks. Route implemented handlers through the Rust evaluator/base registration, add focused stock-R conformance for safe noninteractive behavior, and rerun strict parity.
close_reason: Wired existing Rust handlers for .primTrace/.primUntrace, forceAndCall, declare, environment<-, and standardGeneric through evaluator/base registration; fixed environment<- direct-call argument order and forceAndCall builtin delegation; added stock-R conformance; verified cargo fmt, focused builtin tests, direct forceAndCall runner probe, and strict conformance 479/479.

title: Expose dot-dot-dot introspection primitives
description: GNU R exposes ...elt(n), ...length(), and ...names() as primitives backed by current function dots. The translated primitive table lists them but the Rust evaluator has no handlers, leaving dots introspection unavailable. Implement them against the session-owned environment/dots machinery, add stock-R conformance, and verify strict parity.
close_reason: Implemented ...elt(), ...length(), and ...names() against the current function dots frame, registered them through evaluator/base builtin exposure, added stock-R conformance for length/name/element access, and verified cargo fmt, focused builtin tests, and strict conformance 478/478.

title: Expose .subset and .subset2 internals
description: Why this issue exists: GNU R .subset() and .subset2() primitive internals are present in the translated table but not evaluator-registered, even though Rust [ and [[ handlers already exist. What needs to be done: route .subset/.subset2 to existing subset handlers, add stock-R conformance for atomic/list/language extraction, and verify focused subset tests plus strict conformance.
close_reason: Exposed .subset() and .subset2() through evaluator/base registration by routing them to existing Rust subset handlers, added stock-R conformance for atomic, list, and language extraction paths, and verified cargo fmt, focused mainutils::subset tests, and strict conformance 477/477.

title: Expose .class2 and gc.time primitives
description: Why this issue exists: GNU R primitive entries .class2() and gc.time() remain unreachable. .class2 is needed by methods/class internals and should return class attributes or implicit type class vectors such as c('integer','numeric'); gc.time() should return the current GC timing vector shape. What needs to be done: add Rust handlers/registration, preserve simple GNU output shape, add stock-R conformance, and verify focused tests plus strict conformance.
close_reason: Exposed .class2() and gc.time() through evaluator/base registration, implemented .class2 implicit class vectors and zeroed gc.time timing vector shape, added stock-R conformance, and verified cargo fmt, focused eval::builtin/mainutils::essentials tests, and strict conformance 476/476.

title: Expose as.call and UTF-8 encoding helpers
description: Why this issue exists: GNU R primitive table entries for as.call(), enc2native(), and enc2utf8() are not reachable through evaluator dispatch. as.call already has a Rust implementation, and this UTF-8 runtime can implement enc2native/enc2utf8 as safe character-vector preserving identity helpers for the covered platform policy. What needs to be done: register as.call and encoding helpers, add safe Rust wrappers preserving STRSXP length/NA/names where applicable, add stock-R conformance, and verify focused tests plus strict conformance.
close_reason: Exposed as.call(), enc2native(), and enc2utf8() through evaluator/base registration, implemented UTF-8/native encoding helpers as safe character-vector preserving identity operations for this UTF-8 runtime, fixed do_call pairlist arity to use Rf_length, added stock-R conformance, and verified cargo fmt, focused coerce/essentials/builtin tests, and strict conformance 475/475.

title: Expose remaining core predicate and seq.int primitives
description: Why this issue exists: GNU R primitive table entries for is.complex(), is.raw(), and seq.int() exist, and the Rust code already has the underlying do_is/do_seq implementations, but evaluator dispatch does not expose them, causing unimplemented builtin errors. What needs to be done: register these primitives with the existing Rust handlers, preserve PRIMVAL-driven predicate behavior, add stock-R conformance, and verify focused tests plus strict conformance.
close_reason: Exposed is.complex(), is.raw(), and seq.int() through evaluator dispatch using existing Rust predicate/sequence handlers, extended arithmetic type-name dispatch for complex/raw predicates, added stock-R conformance, and verified cargo fmt, focused eval::builtin/eval::arithmetic tests, and strict conformance 474/474.

title: Wire and harden call primitive
description: Why this issue exists: GNU R's call() primitive is in the translated primitive table and has a Rust do_call port, but evaluator dispatch still reports call as an unimplemented special form. What needs to be done: route call through special/unevaluated dispatch, ensure constructed calls are LANGSXP and preserve evaluated argument/tag behavior, add stock-R conformance for named and positional call construction, and verify focused tests plus strict conformance.
close_reason: Wired GNU R's call() special primitive through Rust unevaluated and special-form dispatch, ensured do_call returns LANGSXP, added stock-R conformance for named/positional call construction and introspection, and verified cargo fmt, focused eval::builtin/mainutils::coerce tests, and strict conformance 473/473.

title: Fix language object length and extraction semantics
description: Why this issue exists: formula dispatch now constructs proper language objects, but probing showed length(~x) returns garbage and as.character(f[[1]]) can hang, which means LANGSXP traversal/extraction is not matching GNU R. What needs to be done: audit the length and [[ paths for LANGSXP/call objects against GNU R behavior, implement safe pairlist traversal for call length and element extraction, add stock-R conformance for formulas and ordinary calls, and verify focused tests plus strict conformance.
close_reason: Fixed LANGSXP/call length and extraction by routing length() and subset indexing through pairlist-aware Rf_length instead of vector XLENGTH, and added direct symbol-to-character coercion so extracted call heads/arguments coerce like GNU R. Added stock-R conformance for formula and ordinary call length/[[ behavior, and verified cargo fmt, focused arithmetic/subset/essentials_basic tests, and strict conformance 472/472.

title: Wire formula tilde primitive through Rust evaluator
description: Why this issue exists: GNU R's ~ operator is present in the translated primitive table and has a faithful do_tilde implementation, but the Rust evaluator special-form dispatch does not route ~, so formula construction depends on incomplete fallback behavior. What needs to be done: dispatch ~ through the Rust evaluator to do_tilde, keep formula class and .Environment semantics aligned with GNU R's names.c, add stock-R conformance for one-sided/two-sided formulas and formula environment/class attributes, and verify focused evaluator tests plus strict conformance.
close_reason: Wired the GNU R formula tilde operator through Rust parser and evaluator dispatch, including one-sided formula syntax, unevaluated primitive dispatch, and special-form routing to do_tilde. Added stock-R conformance for formula class/language shape and .Environment attachment, and verified cargo fmt plus strict conformance 471/471.

title: Expose missing core distribution wrappers
description: Why this issue exists: several GNU R distribution functions have pure Rust numerical cores already ported but are not registered through the evaluator, so qexp(), qpois(), qbinom(), dunif(), punif(), and qunif() fail as unimplemented. What needs to be done: add the Rust builtin wrappers with vectorized argument handling, register them in essentials/evaluator, add stable stock-R conformance coverage, and verify focused tests plus strict conformance.
close_reason: Exposed qexp, qpois, qbinom, dunif, punif, and qunif through Rust evaluator/essentials registration, implemented named and positional argument handling for tail/log flags, added stock-R conformance coverage for default and tail/log paths, and verified cargo fmt, focused eval::builtin/mainutils::essentials tests, and strict conformance 470/470.

title: Implement missing one-argument math builtins
description: Why this issue exists: several GNU R Math1 primitives are present in the translated function table but not dispatched by the Rust evaluator, so calls such as expm1(), log1p(), acosh(), asinh(), atanh(), sinpi(), cospi(), and tanpi() fail as unimplemented. What needs to be done: implement these vectorized numeric functions in Rust using the existing safe SEXP allocation/access patterns, register them in evaluator and essentials registration, add stock-R parity coverage for stable numeric values and NA propagation, and verify focused tests plus strict conformance.
close_reason: Implemented and registered expm1, log1p, acosh, asinh, atanh, sinpi, cospi, and tanpi with vectorized numeric handling, exact pi-cycle cases, NA propagation, stock-R parity coverage, and verified cargo fmt, focused eval::builtin/mainutils::essentials tests, and strict conformance 469/469.

title: Implement .Internal builtins introspection
description: Why this issue exists: names.rs contains the builtins internal entry but do_internal has no handler, so .Internal(builtins(...)) reports unimplemented. GNU R uses this for builtin/internal introspection. What needs to be done: implement a Rust-native handler over the canonical function/evaluator tables, return sorted character names for internal=true and builtin=false, add stable conformance against stock R shape/inclusion properties, and verify focused tests plus strict conformance.
close_reason: Implemented .Internal(builtins(...)) over the canonical Rust function table, returning sorted character vectors for internal-only and all builtin names, added focused table coverage plus stock-R conformance invariants, and verified cargo fmt, mainutils::names tests, and strict conformance 465/465.

title: Fix extSoftVersion primitive table spelling
description: Why this issue exists: the translated names.rs primitive table contains eSoftVersion, but GNU R and the Rust evaluator expose extSoftVersion. This leaves StrToInternal/.Internal metadata inconsistent even though the builtin is callable. What needs to be done: rename the FunTab entry to extSoftVersion, add focused primitive-table coverage, verify focused names/eval tests and strict conformance.
close_reason: Corrected the translated primitive table spelling from eSoftVersion to extSoftVersion, added StrToInternal coverage for the canonical name and stale-name miss, and verified cargo fmt, focused mainutils::names/eval::builtin tests, and strict conformance 464/464.

title: Add Sys.which to translated primitive table
description: Why this issue exists: Sys.which is registered in the Rust evaluator, but the translated names.rs primitive table still lacks the Sys.which FunTab entry, leaving the canonical primitive metadata less faithful to GNU R. What needs to be done: add the Sys.which entry with matching arity/eval metadata near the other Sys.* primitives, add or extend coverage so primitive lookup sees it, verify focused builtin/name tests and strict conformance.
close_reason: Added Sys.which to the translated R_FunTab metadata with matching internal arity/eval fields, covered StrToInternal lookup in mainutils::names tests, and verified cargo fmt, focused eval::builtin/mainutils::names tests, and strict conformance 464/464.

title: Implement Sys.which builtin
description: Why this issue exists: Sys.which is part of GNU R's base system surface but the Rust runtime has no registered builtin for it, so package and user code cannot perform portable PATH lookup. What needs to be done: implement vectorized Sys.which(command) in Rust with GNU-compatible names and empty-string results for commands that are not found, register it in essentials/evaluator, add stable stock-R conformance coverage, and verify strict parity.
close_reason: Implemented and registered Sys.which as a Rust-native vectorized PATH lookup with GNU-compatible names and empty-string misses, added stable stock-R conformance coverage for missing commands, and verified cargo fmt, focused eval::builtin/mainutils::essentials tests, and strict conformance 464/464.

title: Implement path.expand builtin
description: Why this issue exists: path.expand appears in the translated names table but is not registered in the Rust evaluated builtin table, so user code cannot call it. GNU R expands ~ and ~/... using the home directory and leaves ordinary paths unchanged. What needs to be done: implement and register path.expand with vectorized character behavior, add stable stock-R parity coverage, and verify strict conformance.
close_reason: Registered path.expand through the existing platform implementation, added stable stock-R parity coverage for ordinary paths, tilde expansion, ~/ suffix preservation, and vector length, and verified cargo fmt, strict conformance 463/463, plus focused eval::builtin/mainutils::essentials tests.

title: Implement searchpaths helper
description: Why this issue exists: GNU R exposes searchpaths() alongside search(), but the Rust runtime has no searchpaths binding. With attach/search-path handling now implemented, searchpaths() should report stable entries for .GlobalEnv and attached environments. What needs to be done: add a Rust searchpaths() handler, register it, cover stable stock-R behavior without host-specific library path assumptions, and verify strict conformance.
close_reason: Implemented and registered searchpaths() over the Rust search path, added stable GNU R parity coverage for .GlobalEnv and attached environments, and verified cargo fmt, strict conformance 462/462, plus focused eval::builtin/mainutils::essentials tests.

title: Expose attach search-path helper
description: Why this issue exists: mainutils::envir has a do_attach implementation, but attach is not registered in the evaluated builtin table, so user code cannot call attach(). GNU R exposes attach() and it is needed for search-path behavior with find/search/detach. What needs to be done: register attach(), validate the existing handler against stock R for environment attachment/detachment, add conformance coverage, and verify strict parity.
close_reason: Registered attach(), made attach argument handling tag-aware, stored attached environment names in a search()-readable attribute, taught find/as.environment/pos.to.env to traverse attached search-path entries, fixed environmentName for named environments, added stock-R attach/search-path conformance coverage, and verified cargo fmt, eval::builtin/mainutils::essentials tests, and strict conformance 461/461.

title: Implement as.environment search-path conversion
description: Why this issue exists: do_as_environment currently returns .GlobalEnv for every non-environment input, which is not GNU R behavior. GNU R maps numeric positions through pos.to.env and character search-path names such as .GlobalEnv/package:base to their environments. What needs to be done: implement numeric and character search-path conversion, keep environment identity, raise GNU-style invalid position errors, add stock-R parity coverage, and verify strict conformance.
close_reason: Implemented as.environment for environments, numeric search positions, and .GlobalEnv/package:base names; added invalid-name error handling, stock-R parity coverage, and verified cargo fmt, essentials tests, and strict conformance 460/460.

title: Implement pos.to.env search-path lookup
description: Why this issue exists: pos.to.env is present in the base primitive metadata but has no Rust evaluated builtin handler, so calls fail with 'builtin function pos.to.env is not implemented'. GNU R uses it to map search-path positions to environments. What needs to be done: implement pos.to.env for the Rust search path, matching stable GNU R behavior for position 1 and length(search()), add stock-R parity coverage, and verify strict conformance.
close_reason: Implemented pos.to.env over the Rust search path, registered the evaluated builtin handler, added stock-R parity coverage for global/base lookup and invalid positions, and verified cargo fmt, strict conformance 458/458, plus focused builtin and essentials tests.

title: Support find numeric results
description: Why this issue exists: the newly implemented find() covers character search-path results but not GNU R's numeric=TRUE mode. Numeric results are part of base find() behavior and should work for stable cases such as .GlobalEnv-local bindings and missing names. What needs to be done: parse the numeric argument, return named integer positions for matches on the Rust search path, preserve character mode behavior, add stock-R parity coverage for stable numeric cases, and verify strict conformance.
close_reason: Added find(numeric=TRUE) support with named integer results, improved named integer printing for singleton and zero-length vectors, added stable stock-R parity coverage, and verified cargo fmt, strict conformance 456/456, plus focused output/builtin/essentials tests.

title: Implement base find helper
description: Why this issue exists: while validating .GlobalEnv behavior, the stock-R conformance probe for find(".GlobalEnv") could not run because the Rust base environment does not expose find(). GNU R uses find() for search-path introspection and should report package:base for .GlobalEnv. What needs to be done: implement an idiomatic Rust base find() handler using existing environment/search-path helpers, match GNU R for common symbol lookup cases, add stock-R conformance coverage, and verify strict parity.
close_reason: Implemented base find() over the session search path with mode=function handling, registered it in the evaluated builtin table, added stock-R parity coverage for .GlobalEnv/base/global misses, and verified cargo fmt, strict conformance 455/455, and focused eval::builtin/mainutils::essentials unit filters.

title: Fix .GlobalEnv special binding lookup
description: Why this issue exists: the Rust runner currently fails on print(.GlobalEnv) with a malformed SEXP-derived symbol lookup, while GNU R exposes .GlobalEnv as the global environment object. This blocks faithful direct-script behavior and forced the delayedAssign conformance case to avoid .GlobalEnv. What needs to be done: compare the Rust lookup path with GNU R's handling for special environment variables, expose .GlobalEnv through the Rust evaluator/session environment without C-shaped fallback, add stock-R conformance coverage, and verify strict parity.

close_reason: Aligned toString NULL and empty-vector behavior with GNU R.

title: Align dmultinom validation and probability normalization
description: do_dmultinom currently forces zero-length x/prob to length one, silently truncates unequal x/prob lengths, and does not reject invalid or all-zero probabilities before computing. Match GNU R dmultinom length/probability validation and normalize positive probability weights before probability calculation; add strict conformance coverage.
close_reason: Aligned dmultinom validation and probability normalization with GNU R and strict conformance coverage.

title: Import upstream empty vector formatting IO slice
description: Expand tests/upstream-core with a curated GNU R slice covering empty-vector formatting and IO/path helper semantics from r-source/tests/print-tests.R, reg-IO2.R, and reg-tests-1b.R. Keep the slice stock-R comparable with no xfail and document validation in rport-vimr.
close_reason: Imported and validated upstream empty-vector formatting/IO slice with no xfail debt.

title: Preserve zero length filesystem helper outputs
description: Path and filesystem helpers still force XLENGTH(x).max(1), so basename/dirname-style mapping, file.exists, dir.exists, file.create, and nzchar can fabricate length-one results for empty inputs. GNU R preserves empty vectors for these helpers. Remove forced length where output is vector-shaped and add strict conformance coverage.
close_reason: Implemented GNU R zero-length filesystem/path helper behavior with strict conformance coverage.

title: Preserve zero length distribution helper outputs
description: Legacy do_dist_unary and do_dist_tertiary force XLENGTH(x).max(1), so many distribution functions fabricate a length-one result for numeric(0). GNU R returns numeric(0). Remove forced length from those helpers and add strict conformance coverage for representative density, probability, quantile, and hypergeometric/tukey functions.
close_reason: Implemented GNU R zero-length behavior for legacy distribution helpers with strict conformance coverage.

title: Implement pmatch duplicates and empty-string semantics
description: do_pmatch currently forces zero-length inputs to length one, ignores duplicates.ok, treats empty strings as matchable, and lacks explicit NA exact-match behavior. Implement GNU R-style pmatch(x, table, nomatch, duplicates.ok) semantics and add strict conformance coverage.
close_reason: Implemented GNU R pmatch semantics with duplicates.ok and strict conformance coverage.

title: Vectorize charmatch with GNU R match semantics
description: do_charmatch currently treats x as scalar, forces table length to one, ignores nomatch, returns NA for duplicate exact/partial ambiguity where GNU R returns 0, and does not intentionally handle NA exact matching. Implement vectorized charmatch(x, table, nomatch=NA_integer_) semantics and add strict conformance coverage.
close_reason: Implemented vectorized GNU R charmatch semantics with strict conformance coverage.

title: Preserve zero length string primitive outputs
description: nchar(), substr(), trimws(), startsWith(), and endsWith() still force XLENGTH(x).max(1), so empty character inputs can produce length-one outputs and read past empty buffers. GNU R preserves zero-length outputs for these primitives. Remove forced length and add strict conformance coverage.
close_reason: Implemented GNU R zero-length behavior for string primitives with strict conformance coverage.

title: Preserve zero length signif trunc outputs
description: signif() and trunc() still force XLENGTH(x).max(1), causing zero-length inputs to read past buffers and/or return length-one results. GNU R preserves numeric(0). Remove forced length and add strict conformance coverage.
close_reason: Implemented GNU R zero-length behavior for signif/trunc with strict conformance coverage.

title: Preserve zero length abs sign outputs
description: abs() and sign() use XLENGTH(x).max(1), incorrectly turning zero-length inputs into length-one results. GNU R preserves zero length, with abs(integer/logical(0)) returning integer(0) and sign() returning numeric(0). Fix and cover with strict conformance.
close_reason: Implemented GNU R zero-length behavior for abs/sign with strict conformance coverage.

title: Preserve integer type in abs
description: abs() currently coerces integer/logical vectors to REALSXP. GNU R preserves integer output for integer/logical inputs, preserving NA and overflow-as-NA behavior. Implement typed integer/logical abs and add strict conformance coverage.
close_reason: Implemented GNU R integer/logical abs type preservation with strict conformance coverage.

title: Fix which min max missing handling
description: which.min()/which.max() currently seed from the first element, only skip NA bit-patterns, and return scalar 0 when no finite candidate exists. GNU R skips NA/NaN and returns integer(0) for all-missing/non-comparable inputs. Implement option-based scanning and add strict conformance coverage.
close_reason: Implemented GNU R missing-value behavior for which.min/which.max with strict conformance coverage.

title: Use shared missing predicate for anyNA helpers
description: anyNA()/allNA() duplicate incomplete missing-value checks: character NA is detected only through null pointers and real NaN is not treated like is.na. Reuse the typed atomic missing predicate and add strict conformance coverage for character NA and NaN.
close_reason: Implemented anyNA/allNA missing-value parity via shared typed predicate with strict conformance coverage.

title: Fix finite infinite nan predicate shapes
description: is.finite(), is.infinite(), and is.nan() currently return scalar TRUE/FALSE for unsupported atomic types. GNU R returns a logical vector matching input length, with character values false and integer/logical finite except NA. Implement shape-correct predicates and strict conformance coverage.
close_reason: Implemented GNU R-shaped finite/infinite/nan predicate vectors with strict conformance coverage.

title: Honor character NA in complete cases
description: complete.cases() and is_complete() only treat numeric/logical missing values as incomplete. Character NA should be incomplete as in GNU R. Add strict conformance coverage for character vectors and mixed arguments.
close_reason: Implemented character NA handling for complete.cases/is_complete with strict conformance coverage.

title: Implement atomic na.omit na.exclude attributes
description: na.omit() currently drops numeric NAs without names or na.action metadata, ignores character missing values, and na.exclude returns class omit. Implement atomic vector omission for logical/integer/real/character/raw-compatible copying where applicable, preserve names, and attach GNU R-like na.action with omit/exclude class.
close_reason: Implemented atomic na.omit/na.exclude value, name, and na.action class parity with strict conformance coverage.

title: Implement head tail character and list copying
description: head() and tail() allocate result vectors for all types but only copy numeric/logical payloads, leaving character and list results uninitialized and dropping names. Implement typed element copying and names slicing for STRSXP, VECSXP/EXPRSXP, RAWSXP, and existing numeric atomics with strict parity coverage.
close_reason: Implemented safe typed head()/tail() copying for character/list/raw values with names parity coverage.

title: Implement rev character and list element copying
description: rev() allocates an output vector for any type but only copies real/integer/logical payloads, leaving character and list-like results uninitialized. Implement typed element copying for character and VECSXP results and cover GNU R parity.
close_reason: Implemented safe typed rev() copying for character/list/raw values with names parity coverage.

title: Implement character set operation parity
description: setdiff(), union(), intersect(), and setequal() currently key through integer/real buffers and are only correct for numeric atomics. Implement Rust-shaped atomic key handling for same-type character vectors, preserving GNU R order and NA behavior, with strict conformance coverage.
close_reason: Implemented character set-operation parity with typed atomic keys and strict conformance coverage.

title: Implement unique atomic type and argument parity
description: unique() currently returns non-numeric atomic vectors unchanged and ignores fromLast/incomparables named arguments. Implement GNU R-compatible behavior for logical, integer, real, and character atomics while keeping the code Rust-shaped and covered by strict conformance.
close_reason: Implemented atomic unique() GNU R parity for character/logical/integer/real vectors with strict conformance coverage.

title: Fix duplicated fromLast semantics
description: duplicated(x, fromLast=TRUE) should scan from the end and mark earlier occurrences as duplicates. The current implementation appears to mark forward duplicates instead. Add character/numeric/NA conformance and keep anyDuplicated fromLast behavior covered.
close_reason: Implemented GNU R duplicated/anyDuplicated fromLast and incomparables=NA semantics with strict parity coverage.

title: Align sort.list with order NA semantics
description: sort.list should return order indices with GNU R na.last and decreasing behavior for atomic vectors. The current implementation needs inspection and likely should share typed order semantics for logical/integer/real/character inputs.
close_reason: Aligned sort.list with typed order semantics, including character/logical vectors, decreasing, na.last placement, and compressed indices for na.last=NA; added strict conformance 343_sort_list_na_last. Validation: focused essentials test target, strict conformance 349/349, strict clippy, diff check.

title: Support rank ties.method variants
description: do_rank now handles typed keys and na.last but still uses average ties unconditionally. Implement deterministic GNU R tie methods average, first, last, min, and max for atomic vectors; leave random out until RNG-sensitive parity is deliberately designed.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic rank ties.method variants average, first, last, min, and max; added strict conformance 342_rank_ties_method. Validation: focused essentials test target, strict conformance 348/348, strict clippy, diff check.

title: Support rank na.last and character keys
description: do_rank currently coerces through elt_real_safe, has a fixed missing policy, and does not rank character vectors. Implement GNU R-compatible rank(x, na.last=TRUE/FALSE/NA) for atomic logical/integer/real/character vectors with average ties, preserving output shape/removal behavior.
close_reason: Implemented typed rank() with GNU R average-tie ranks and na.last placement/removal for logical, integer, real, and character vectors; added strict conformance 341_rank_na_last_character. Validation: focused essentials test target, strict conformance 347/347, strict clippy, diff check.

title: Support order na.last semantics
description: do_order currently sorts numeric values with a fixed missing-value policy and ignores GNU R's na.last argument. Implement NA placement/removal for order(..., na.last=TRUE/FALSE/NA) while preserving decreasing behavior for non-missing values.
close_reason: Implemented typed order() index construction with GNU R na.last placement/removal semantics and character/logical support; added strict conformance 340_order_na_last. Validation: focused essentials test target, strict conformance 346/346, strict clippy, diff check.

title: Print zero-length atomic vectors like GNU R
description: The output layer currently renders at least logical(0) as an empty indexed line '[1]' instead of GNU R's typed zero-length form such as logical(0). Implement stock-R-style printing for zero-length atomic vectors and cover logical/integer/double/character/raw/complex where supported.
close_reason: Implemented GNU R typed zero-length atomic printing across default output and type-specific print helpers; added strict conformance 339_print_zero_length_atomic. Validation: focused output and essentials tests, strict conformance 345/345, strict clippy, diff check.

title: Make ifelse result length follow test length
description: do_ifelse currently uses the maximum length of test/yes/no, but GNU R returns a vector shaped like test and recycles yes/no into that shape. Implement test-length result semantics, including zero-length test behavior, while preserving typed branch output.
close_reason: Implemented GNU R-compatible ifelse result length semantics and zero-length branch handling; added strict conformance 338_ifelse_test_length. Validation: focused essentials_basic test target, strict conformance 344/344, strict clippy, diff check.

title: Fix character branches in ifelse parity
description: Character-valued ifelse(test, yes, no) currently degrades selected strings to NA in at least the sort NA conformance scenario. Implement GNU R-compatible branch selection for character vectors while preserving existing numeric/logical behavior.
close_reason: Implemented typed ifelse result allocation and branch copying for character, real, integer, and logical outputs; added strict conformance 337_ifelse_character_branches. Validation: focused essentials_basic test target, strict conformance 343/343, strict clippy, diff check.

title: Fix deparse for quoted language calls
description: deparse(quote(sum(1, 2))) currently prints "6" in the Rust runtime instead of stock GNU R's call text. This surfaced while adding substitute() coverage, so keep it tracked separately from the promise lookup fix. Acceptance: deparse(quote(sum(1, 2))), deparse(quote(1 + 2)), and substitute() of call arguments match stock R without forcing or evaluating the language object.
notes: 2026-05-01: Routed essentials::do_deparse through the real mainutils::deparse implementation instead of the old elt_to_string shortcut. Added fixture 264_deparse_language_calls covering deparse(quote(sum(1, 2))), deparse(quote(1 + 2)), substitute() call arguments, and deparse1. Strict conformance passes 269/269.
close_reason: Fixed language-call deparse and added strict parity coverage.

title: Run release-gated full signoff matrix
description: Why this exists: after core compatibility beads close, the project needs an end-to-end shippability check across Rust tests, conformance parity, upstream slices, Android build, UniFFI bindings, and desktop embedding smoke. What needs doing: run the full matrix, fix blockers, and record residual known gaps.

title: Complete complex hyperbolic and NaN formatting parity
description: Why this exists: rport-84cp has core complex arithmetic landed, but upstream complex.R still has gaps around sinh/cosh/tanh branch behavior, NaN/NA formatting, fft/polyroot scope, and edge output. What needs doing: compare against stock GNU R and close the remaining complex arithmetic/reporting gaps without C-shaped shortcuts.
acceptance_criteria: Expanded upstream complex slice covers hyperbolic functions and representative NaN/NA formatting; Rust output matches stock R for supported scope; out-of-scope fft/polyroot work is either implemented or tracked with explicit dependencies.
notes: Implemented complex sinh/cosh/tanh in Rust complex arithmetic and wired real/complex hyperbolic functions through do_math1 and builtin registration. tanh uses a stable large-real branch so tanh(356+0i) matches stock R instead of overflowing. Expanded upstream complex slice with hyperbolic identities and representative NaN complex formatting; added conformance case 221_complex_hyperbolic_nan. Updated README release proof to 226/226 conformance and 14/14 upstream slices. Validation: cargo fmt --all; cargo fmt --check --all; git diff --check; cargo test -p rmath eval::complex_arith -- --test-threads=1; Rscript --vanilla tests/upstream-core/cases/011_complex_arithmetic_identities.R; single Rust runner for 221_complex_hyperbolic_nan; scripts/upstream_core_slices.sh --report target/codex-upstream-after-complex-hyperbolic (14/14); scripts/conformance_parity.sh --check --strict --report target/codex-conformance-after-complex-hyperbolic (226/226).
close_reason: Complex hyperbolic functions and NaN formatting coverage are implemented with green upstream and conformance gates.

title: Complete pure-R package data serialization path
description: Why this exists: package loading works for pure-R namespaces and system.file lookup, but serialization/lazy data remains incomplete for full GNU R compatibility and Android package use. What needs doing: support practical pure-R package data files, define lazy-data behavior, and make unsupported serialized native forms fail with typed policy errors.
acceptance_criteria: Package data loading works for representative pure-R/serialized data cases needed by Android subset; lazy data behavior is deterministic; unsupported native/binary package artifacts produce explicit policy errors.
close_reason: Implemented source-form package data and source LazyData support, preserved explicit serialized/lazy DB policy errors, expanded Android/embed corpus proof, and validated with package corpus, conformance, and upstream slice gates.

title: Use deparser-backed dput/deparse1 round-trips
description: Why this exists: dget now reads/parses/evaluates source, but dput() and deparse1() still use elt_to_string placeholders, so language objects and vectors do not round-trip like GNU R. What needs doing: route dput/deparse1 through the deparse engine, honor file output for practical embedded use, and add stock-R parity cases for simple calls, vectors, and NULL.
acceptance_criteria: dput/deparse1 no longer use placeholder stringification for core expression/vector cases; conformance parity includes stock-R round-trip fixtures; existing parser/deparser tests remain green.
notes: Implemented deparser-backed deparse1() and dput(). deparse1() now joins real deparse engine output with the requested collapse string instead of using elt_to_string placeholders. dput() now deparses objects, writes to captured stdout or a file path, and returns the original object for visible print behavior. Added conformance case 217_dput_deparse1_roundtrip covering language deparse, vector deparse, and dput -> dget file round-trip. Validation: cargo fmt --all; cargo fmt --check --all; git diff --check; cargo test -p rmath mainutils::essentials:: -- --test-threads=1; scripts/conformance_parity.sh --check --strict --report target/codex-conformance-after-dput (222/222); scripts/upstream_core_slices.sh --report target/codex-upstream-after-dput (14/14).
close_reason: Implemented deparser-backed deparse1/dput with stock-R parity fixture and green validation.

title: Implement bquote substitution semantics
description: Why this exists: bquote() still returns the expression unchanged. What needs doing: implement .() substitution over language trees using caller environment lookup/eval, preserve quoted structure, handle nested calls and basic list/vector expressions, and compare against stock GNU R.
acceptance_criteria: bquote() substitutes .(expr) values like GNU R for core language cases; unsupported edge cases error explicitly rather than silently returning unchanged expressions; conformance parity covers substitution and non-substitution paths.
notes: Implemented core bquote substitution. bquote is now handled as an unevaluated builtin so arguments are not evaluated before the handler. The handler walks LANGSXP/LISTSXP trees, evaluates only .(...) calls in the caller environment, preserves tags/named arguments, and returns a rebuilt quoted language tree. Added conformance case 219_bquote_substitution covering arithmetic substitution and named call arguments. Validation: cargo fmt --all; cargo fmt --check --all; git diff --check; cargo test -p rmath eval::builtin:: -- --test-threads=1; cargo test -p rmath mainutils::essentials:: -- --test-threads=1; scripts/conformance_parity.sh --check --strict --report target/codex-conformance-after-bquote (224/224); scripts/upstream_core_slices.sh --report target/codex-upstream-after-bquote (14/14).
close_reason: Implemented bquote .(...) substitution for core language trees with stock-R parity fixture and green validation.

title: Fix substitute() promise lookup inside braced closure bodies
description: substitute() currently returns the formal symbol rather than the original actual expression when called inside a braced closure body, e.g. g <- function(x) { deparse(substitute(x)) }; g(any) returns "x" instead of stock R's "any". The non-braced body path works, so this likely lives in begin/special evaluation context or promise visibility across braced body evaluation. Acceptance: braced and non-braced closure bodies both preserve PRCODE for substitute(), and upstream any-all helper can use the original braced check_case shape.
notes: 2026-05-01: Fixed nondeterministic substitute() promise lookup. Root cause was do_substitute using vector LENGTH() on a pairlist to detect the optional env argument, which sometimes treated an absent env as present and evaluated it to NULL. Replaced that with pairlist CDR() detection; routed the old essentials substitute stub to the real coerce implementation; consolidated symbol-name equality for environment/eval/formal matching. Added fixture 263_substitute_promise_lookup; strict conformance passes 268/268.
close_reason: Fixed substitute() promise lookup nondeterminism and added strict parity coverage.

title: Fix higher-order any/all/do.call/list-input parity
description: The expanded upstream any-all slice exposed a Rust evaluator failure () when checking any()/all() through helper closures and do.call/list inputs. Implement the missing function argument/substitute/deparse/do.call behavior and restore the full r-source/tests/any-all.R-derived list-input coverage.
notes: Completed higher-order any/all helper parity: substitute/quote now dispatch as unevaluated special forms, symbol deparse no longer uses vector length, identical() is registered and handles default controls, c() preserves list concatenation/names, and do.call() maps named list args such as na.rm to tags. Expanded upstream any-all slice now covers helper closures, do.call(list inputs), and named na.rm. Validation: cargo fmt --check --all; cargo test -p rmath eval:: -- --test-threads=1; cargo test -p rmath mainutils::essentials:: -- --test-threads=1; scripts/upstream_core_slices.sh --report target/codex-upstream-after-substitute (14/14); scripts/conformance_parity.sh --check --strict --report target/codex-conformance-after-substitute (216/216).
close_reason: Higher-order any/all/do.call/list-input parity is implemented and covered by expanded upstream any-all slice; strict conformance and upstream gates pass.

title: Support upstream complex literal syntax and broader complex math parity
description: The expanded upstream slice from r-source/tests/complex.R failed on parser syntax such as 0i/1i before reaching complex math checks. Implement R's complex literal parsing and then grow the complex upstream slice to cover powers, trig/hyperbolic branch behavior, NaN formatting, fft/polyroot where in scope, and stock-R output parity.
notes: Parser complex literals were already landed. Expanded runtime parity now also handles complex c() construction, sqrt/log/exp, sin/cos/tan, abs/Mod/Arg/Re/Im/Conj registration, and fixes complex tangent via sin(z)/cos(z). Expanded upstream complex slice covers powers plus these core complex operations against stock R tolerance checks. Validation: cargo fmt --check --all; cargo test -p rmath eval::complex_arith -- --test-threads=1; cargo test -p rmath mainutils::essentials:: -- --test-threads=1; scripts/upstream_core_slices.sh --report target/codex-upstream-after-complex-expanded (14/14); scripts/conformance_parity.sh --check --strict --report target/codex-conformance-after-complex-expanded (216/216). Remaining r-source complex.R scope: hyperbolic branch behavior, NaN formatting details, fft/polyroot where in scope.
close_reason: Complex literal syntax and broader complex arithmetic parity are implemented; child hyperbolic/NaN formatting bead rport-se69 is closed; upstream_core_slices passes 14/14 and strict conformance passes 277/277 after current parser cleanup.

title: Complete structure/deparse attribute remapping parity
description: The expanded structure.R-derived slice exposed evaluator/deparse/attribute remapping gaps () around structure(.Dim/.Dimnames/.Label), attributes(), and factor storage behavior. Port the stock-R structure/deparse remapping semantics and add upstream parity fixtures.
close_reason: Implemented structure()/attributes() builtin parity for the covered upstream structure slice. structure() now attaches attributes and remaps stock-R dotted names .Dim, .Dimnames, .Names, .Tsp, and .Label; attributes() returns a named list. Expanded 010_structure_attribute_remap with names, attributes, dim/dimnames remapping, and factor .Label/class preservation. title: Support base primitive registry introspection environments
description: The expanded upstream primitive-accounting slice from r-source/tests/primitives.R cannot yet parse/evaluate base:: qualified primitive lookups and .GenericArgsEnv/.ArgsEnv/tools::langElts accounting. Implement the missing parser/runtime pieces and verify primitive generic/non-generic registries against stock GNU R.

Remaining full primitives.R scope still includes complete primitive accounting membership and methods/S4 checks beyond this runtime subset.

description: Build a curated importer/harness for upstream GNU R tests that are relevant to the Rust runtime core.
