acceptance_criteria: Curated upstream test slices run through scripts/conformance_parity.sh or a sibling harness; unsupported upstream expectations are documented as xfail beads; release gate documents when to run the imported suite.
close_reason: Added scripts/upstream_core_slices.sh sibling harness, 5 curated upstream GNU R core slices with xfail metadata, release-gate/docs integration, and fixed R power identity parity found by the imported slice. Validation: scripts/conformance_parity.sh --check --report target/arithmetic-parity-conformance; scripts/upstream_core_slices.sh --report target/upstream-core-slices; cargo test -p rmath --lib -- --test-threads=1; cargo clippy -p rmath --all-targets -- -D warnings; git diff --check.

title: Shrink SEXP unsafe internals and split object module
description: Keep Sexp<'a>, RArena, and RSession as the Rust-shaped ownership model, but reduce internal C-shaped surface. Split sexp/object/mod.rs into typed vector, pairlist, attributes, symbol, and conversion modules; replace numeric tag tables with SEXPTYPE matches; narrow unsafe constructors to owner-checked boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: No public safe API exposes raw SEXP; object modules are focused; unsafe blocks are smaller and documented; Sexp::from_raw remains crate-private or is replaced by owner-scoped constructors; existing safety/conformance gates pass.
notes: Completed SEXP object split: moved type/view predicates to kind.rs, raw slot accessors to slots.rs, vector element/slice/mutation/iterator accessors to vector.rs, and kept object/mod.rs focused on Sexp ownership, checked raw wrapping, shared guards, pairlist helpers, identity/display, and tests. Tightened public Rust-facing API by making GenericVector/PairlistBuilder raw mutators crate-local and removing deprecated public raw aliases; RSession raw eval helpers are crate-local while typed Sexp/source-code eval paths remain public. Validation: focused object tests, focused session tests, clippy -D warnings, 211/211 conformance, 5/5 upstream slices, full rmath lib tests 1941 passed / 4 ignored, diff check clean.
close_reason: Completed SEXP object module split, narrowed raw public API seams, and passed focused/full/parity quality gates.

title: Make evaluator dispatch Rust-shaped and modular
description: Refactor rmath-rs/rmath/src/eval/eval.rs away from a single 6k-line C-port dispatcher. Split primitive metadata, special forms, closures/promises, builtin dispatch, visibility, and error/control-flow into focused modules while preserving GNU R behavior and existing conformance.
acceptance_criteria: eval.rs loses the broad unsafe_op allow or has it narrowed to small modules; builtin dispatch is table/module driven; PRIMPRINT/visibility and promise forcing have focused tests; conformance remains green.
notes: Progress: canonicalized primitive identity before descriptor-driven dispatch. Base registration now uses eval::primitive::make_primitive_binding, which creates canonical R_FunTab primitives only when the table argument policy matches the installed binding, and marks .Internal/Rust-only helper bindings with PRIMOFFSET=-1. eval::apply now prefers PrimitiveDescriptor names and falls back to call-head names only for noncanonical helpers. Added regression coverage for canonical +/if bindings, noncanonical log/helper bindings, and base-env primitive identity. Fixed require() visibility to match stock R invisibility. Validation: cargo test -p rmath eval:: -- --test-threads=1; cargo test -p rmath --lib -- --test-threads=1 (1932 passed, 4 ignored); cargo clippy -p rmath --all-targets -- -D warnings; scripts/conformance_parity.sh --check --report target/primitive-identity-conformance (207/207). Remaining: replace the evaluated builtin string match with a generated/table-driven handler map.
close_reason: Completed evaluator dispatch modularization: apply.rs now coordinates closure/special/builtin application through PrimitiveCall and visibility helpers, eval::builtin owns unevaluated/evaluated handler tables (590 evaluated handlers, duplicate/coverage tests), primitive identity is descriptor-first via canonical R_FunTab bindings with noncanonical helpers marked PRIMOFFSET=-1, and eval/builtin unsafe boundaries deny unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn. Validation: cargo test -p rmath eval:: -- --test-threads=1 (157 passed); cargo test -p rmath --lib -- --test-threads=1 (1936 passed, 4 ignored); cargo clippy -p rmath --all-targets -- -D warnings; scripts/conformance_parity.sh --check --report target/builtin-table-conformance (207/207).

title: Stress Android parallel sessions without shared mutable runtime state
description: Prove the Android-facing runtime can run multiple independent R sessions in parallel tabs/threads. Audit remaining atomics/thread-locals/globals, distinguish per-token atomics from process globals, and add stress tests for independent sessions, cancellation, package paths, and plots.
acceptance_criteria: Parallel-session stress tests run host-side and in Android smoke where practical; docs explain the remaining thread_local current-instance bridge; no process-global mutable interpreter state is required for ordinary Android session use.
close_reason: Completed host-side Android parallel session stress slice: core RSession is now compile-time thread-confined with a zero-sized Rc PhantomData marker, Android tests run 4 worker-owned sessions in parallel and verify isolated globals, RNG sequences, per-session path/package/tempdir policy, and scoped cancellation. Audit docs now explain the remaining thread_local current-instance bridge and clarify that the only atomic in ordinary Android path is an optional per-call cancellation token, not process-global mutable interpreter state. Validation: cargo test -p rmath test_parallel_android_sessions_stress_isolated_state_paths_and_cancellation -- --test-threads=1; cargo test -p rmath android::tests:: -- --test-threads=1 (82 passed); cargo test -p rmath --lib -- --test-threads=1 (1937 passed, 4 ignored); cargo clippy -p rmath --all-targets -- -D warnings; scripts/conformance_parity.sh --check --report target/android-session-isolation-conformance (207/207).

title: Android hard resource limits
description: Add host-owned CPU, heap, allocation, and wall-clock resource budgets for Android sessions before accepting arbitrary untrusted R code. Current cooperative cancellation is implemented, but hard quotas are documented as a remaining sandbox gap.
close_reason: Added Android-facing per-session resource limit API for eval depth, cooperative wall-clock checks, arena bytes, and arena node count; wired normal eval to start limit timing; documented preemptive CPU enforcement as host policy; full release gate passed.

title: Remove raw pairlist builder outputs from Rust call sites
description: Why: pairlist builder APIs still return/push raw SEXP values, keeping closure and dispatch argument logic in raw-pointer mode. What: add typed finish variants and migrate Rust callers to Sexp-returning APIs until explicit raw boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: Pairlist builder has typed finish APIs for common pairlist/dots/lang outputs; closure/dispatch callers no longer need raw builder output; builder/object/eval tests pass.
close_reason: Typed pairlist builder finish APIs are in place; closure and dispatch call sites now use typed Sexp pushes/finishes; full release gate passed.

title: Remove process-global workspace name state
description: Why: startup.rs stores WORKSPACE_NAME in an AtomicPtr shared by all interpreter instances. What: replace it with session-owned startup/workspace metadata or a pure owned Rust value scoped to RInstance.
acceptance_criteria: Workspace name read/write paths do not share mutable process-global state across RSession instances; same-thread and parallel session tests prove no bleed; Android mutable-global audit remains green.
notes: Moved workspace name from process-global AtomicPtr into per-instance StartupRuntimeState owned by RInstance. get/set workspace name now dispatch through current RInstance; focused workspace_name_is_session_local regression passes and proves same-thread instance switching does not bleed state.
close_reason: Workspace name is now per-RInstance StartupRuntimeState, Android global allowlist entry removed, same-thread isolation regression and full release gate pass.

title: Move timezone runtime cache into session-owned state
description: Why: support/tzone.rs still uses a process-global OnceLock<Mutex<TzGlobals>>, so parallel R sessions share mutable timezone state. What: relocate timezone parse/cache state behind RInstance/RSession ownership or an explicit host-global policy if it is truly process state.
acceptance_criteria: Timezone mutable cache is no longer process-global interpreter state; parallel/session-isolation tests cover time/date evaluation; Android mutable-global audit remains green.
notes: Moved compiled tzone cache from process-global OnceLock<Mutex<TzGlobals>> into RInstance::tzone_state. Public timezone entrypoints now dispatch through the active instance. The inactive support/tzone copy no longer uses process-global state; its fallback cache is thread-local. Added test_tzone_cache_is_session_local_on_same_thread. Focused tzone tests pass.
close_reason: Compiled timezone cache is now RInstance-owned, support copy no longer uses process-global cache, focused isolation test and full release gate pass.

title: Make evaluator assignment use typed Environment
description: Why: normal assignment is core evaluator behavior and still writes through raw defineVar/setVar. What: migrate assign_to_symbol and applydefine-style paths to Environment/Sexp handles where binding-location semantics do not require raw varloc APIs.
acceptance_criteria: Core assignment paths use Environment for environment binding/update instead of raw defineVar/setVar where semantics permit; assignment integration and conformance tests pass.
notes: Migrated eval::assignment binding writes through bind_assignment, which validates raw inputs into Sexp handles and uses Environment::define/set. eval/assignment.rs no longer imports raw defineVar/setVar. cargo test -p rmath assignment -- --test-threads=1 passes.
close_reason: eval::assignment writes now route through typed Environment, assignment tests and full release gate pass.

title: Make protection index API typed and Rust-shaped
description: Why: protect.rs still exposes raw protection index and raw SEXP protect/reprotect entrypoints to Rust callers. What: introduce typed protection slot handles and migrate Rust code to typed guard APIs, leaving raw functions as legacy shims only.
acceptance_criteria: Typed protection-index handle exists; Rust callers stop manufacturing raw ProtectIndex pointers; protect/session/eval tests cover re-protect and unwind behavior.
close_reason: Added typed ProtectionSlot/IndexedProtectGuard APIs, migrated apply/optim off raw protect-index pointers, kept legacy shims isolated, and passed the full release gate.

title: Wire .Machine initialization through typed Environment
description: Why: mainutils::machine still carries a raw defineVar wrapper and leaves Init_R_Machine's environment binding commented out, which is neither faithful to R nor Rust-shaped. What: replace the raw wrapper with typed Environment/Sexp validation, define .Machine when rho is an environment, and cover the binding with a focused test.
acceptance_criteria: Init_R_Machine defines .Machine in a real environment via Environment facade; raw local defineVar shim is removed; focused test proves the binding and names exist; relevant tests pass.
notes: Implemented define_machine_binding using typed Environment/Sexp handles. Init_R_Machine now installs .Machine into valid environment arguments instead of constructing an unreachable value. Focused test test_init_machine_defines_machine_binding passes and verifies names.
close_reason: Init_R_Machine now installs .Machine via typed Environment, focused test verifies binding and names, and full release gate passed.

title: Add typed Environment facade and migrate session bindings
description: Why: C compatibility is not a design goal, but environment lookup/binding still encourages raw defineVar/R_findVar call paths. What: introduce a typed Environment facade over owner-scoped Sexp handles, migrate RSession find/define and safe closure binding to it, and keep raw functions as legacy shims.
acceptance_criteria: Typed Environment facade exists; RSession find/define and at least one eval safe path use it instead of raw defineVar/R_findVar; focused tests and full release gate pass.
notes: Added sexp::envir::Environment typed facade with find/find_in_frame/define/set/exists methods. Migrated RSession::find_var/define_var and eval::closure::apply_closure_safe binding loop off raw R_findVar/defineVar. Focused Environment and session binding tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented typed Environment facade, migrated RSession find/define and closure binding path to it, and passed full release gate.

title: Make vector and pairlist builders Rust-first
description: Why: builder docs and tests still make raw SEXP slots look like the natural API even though C compatibility is not a design goal. What: make typed Sexp-based builder methods and examples the primary path, rename raw mutators as raw/legacy helpers, migrate tests and obvious call sites.
acceptance_criteria: Builder examples/tests use owner-scoped Sexp handles; raw builder mutators are explicitly legacy/raw named; focused builder tests and release gate pass.
notes: Release gate initially caught doctests using private raw Sexp::from_raw. Added safe public Sexp::nil() and updated builder examples to use it. rmath doctests pass.
close_reason: Made builder APIs Rust-first with typed constructors/mutators, added Sexp::nil, migrated builder/pairlist tests and docs off raw construction, and passed full release gate.

title: Replace raw protect ergonomics with typed session-owned guards
description: Why: we no longer want C compatibility to drive internal API shape. The protection stack is session-owned, but the easiest API still accepts raw SEXP pointers. What: add typed Sexp-based protect/preserve helpers, migrate core tests and obvious internal call sites away from raw protect ergonomics, keep legacy raw shims as compatibility islands only where still needed.
acceptance_criteria: Typed Sexp protect/preserve helpers exist; at least one current raw protect call path is migrated; tests and release gate pass.
notes: Added typed protect_sexp and preserve_sexp guards around owner-scoped Sexp handles; raw protect helper is now labelled legacy. protect.rs now denies unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn. Focused sexp::protect tests pass.
close_reason: Added typed Sexp-based protect/preserve guards, migrated protection tests to owner-scoped values, locked protect.rs with unsafe_op deny, and passed full release gate.

title: Make multi-instance runtime state explicitly session-owned
description: Why: Android tabs need parallel R sessions without global-style runtime state. Thread-local/current-instance shims are useful compatibility boundaries, but app-facing and internal Rust paths should prefer explicit session/arena handles. What: audit remaining current-instance/global/static state, classify compatibility-only vs runtime-owned, and migrate one state family at a time to explicit RSession/RInstance ownership.
acceptance_criteria: Audit documents remaining global/thread-local state classes; at least one runtime state family migrates or gains explicit owner validation; parallel-session tests and Android checks pass.
notes: Added explicit session-owned eval-limit and cancellation facades in rmath::sexp::RSession; routed Android/r-embed cancellation eval through a scoped owner-restoring API; added runtime-state audit doc; focused session, Android, and r-embed cancellation tests plus Android global allowlist pass.
close_reason: Added runtime-state audit documentation, explicit session-owned eval limit and cancellation facades, scoped Android/r-embed cancellation evaluation, and tests proving per-session isolation; full release gate passed.

title: Convert SEXP compatibility layers into explicit safe internal facades
description: Why: accessors.rs/constructors.rs/memory_ext.rs/attrib/context still expose C-shaped raw APIs, which is acceptable for compatibility but not ideal for internal Rust code. What: add or promote safe internal facades for common object construction, attribute access, context/protect handling, and pairlist/vector mutation; migrate high-traffic internal call sites.
acceptance_criteria: New or promoted safe facades cover common internal use; at least one high-traffic eval/sexp call path no longer reaches raw accessors directly; tests and clippy pass.
notes: 2026-04-25: added IntVector::sequence and int_sequence_current safe builder facade, then migrated eval::defaults::seq_int off manual Rf_allocVector3/set_integer_elt construction. Focused builder/defaults tests pass; release gate passed: strict clippy, full tests, Android aarch64, 201/201 conformance, safe API audit, and git diff --check.
close_reason: Safe builder facade added and seq_int migrated; release gate passed.

title: Shrink crate-level unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn allowance
description: Why: the crate-level unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn allow is the clearest remaining safety smell. What: measure warning counts by module, move allowance to the smallest legacy modules that still need it, and clean selected core modules so they compile without the crate-level allowance.
acceptance_criteria: Root lib.rs no longer carries a blanket unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn allow, or it is replaced by a documented temporary module-level allowlist with measured counts; strict clippy and release gate pass.
notes: Moved unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn from the rmath crate root into measured module-level legacy allows. Added docs/unsafe-op-allowlist.tsv with 125 modules and 24,716 measured warnings from scripts/unsafe_op_report.sh. Root lib.rs now points to the allowlist instead of carrying the blanket lint allow.
close_reason: Removed root unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn allow, added measured module-level legacy allowlist for remaining translated unsafe boundaries, and passed full release gate.

title: Decompose eval.rs into Rust-shaped evaluation phases
description: Why: eval.rs is still too C-shaped and too large, with raw SEXP procedural flow across classification, dispatch, builtins, closures, and result visibility. What: introduce small internal modules/types for expression classification, dispatch target resolution, builtin/special/closure application, and visibility/result handling while preserving the public R-compatible entry points.
acceptance_criteria: Core eval flow has named Rust modules or helper types for classification/dispatch/apply/result; behavior-preserving tests and conformance stay green; raw SEXP use is reduced in the central eval path.
notes: 2026-04-25: introduced EvalKind and classify_expr in eval.rs, making the safe evaluator's central decision tree an explicit classify-then-dispatch phase boundary. Added classifier tests for self-evaluating, symbol, and language call expressions. Release gate passed: strict clippy, full tests, Android aarch64, 201/201 conformance, safe API audit, and git diff --check.
close_reason: Initial Rust-shaped eval phase boundary landed and release gate passed.

title: Move numeric SEXP views into reusable Rust-shaped module
description: Why: arithmetic.rs now has a good typed NumericVector abstraction, but keeping it private makes other eval/stats code repeat raw REAL/INTEGER/LOGICAL access. What: move the numeric/logical vector view into a reusable sexp/eval-safe module with exact-type access, recycling helpers, NA coercion, and typed setters where appropriate; update arithmetic to consume it without behavior drift.
acceptance_criteria: Reusable internal numeric vector view exists outside arithmetic.rs; arithmetic uses it; focused arithmetic/defaults tests pass; strict clippy passes.
notes: 2026-04-25: extracted arithmetic's NumericVector into sexp::numeric as a reusable internal Rust-shaped numeric/logical SEXP view. Arithmetic now imports the shared view and uses recycled_len_with; new tests cover non-numeric rejection, integer/logical real coercion, and recycling length/index behavior. Release gate passed: strict clippy, full tests, Android aarch64, 201/201 conformance, safe API audit, and git diff --check.
close_reason: Reusable numeric SEXP view extracted and release gate passed.

title: Shrink legacy unsafe-op lint boundary with audited safe wrappers
description: Strict clippy now passes by documenting the existing C-port unsafe boundary at crate level. That is a useful baseline, but it is not the final Rust-shaped safety story. Move high-traffic legacy modules toward narrow unsafe blocks, safe SEXP/arena/session APIs, and documented invariants without sacrificing C source diffability. Start with eval/session/sexp memory paths, then numeric/library modules where Android-facing code crosses into legacy pointers.
acceptance_criteria: Unsafe operations in selected core modules are contained in small audited blocks or safe helper APIs; crate-level unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn allow is reduced or scoped; release gate remains green with strict clippy and conformance.
notes:
2026-04-25: release gate passed after the RSession owner-boundary refactor: strict clippy default gate, rmath/r-embed/r-uniffi tests, Android aarch64 checks, 201/201 conformance, safe API audit, and git diff --check all green.
2026-04-25: arithmetic core moved from C-shaped raw REAL/INTEGER/LOGICAL pointer loops to a Rust-shaped NumericVector view plus Sexp setters across binary arithmetic, comparisons, unary math, summaries, mean, and scalar logical arguments. Release gate passed after the refactor: strict clippy, rmath/r-embed/r-uniffi tests, Android aarch64 checks, 201/201 conformance, safe API audit, and git diff --check all green.
2026-04-25: evaluator defaults cleanup fixed seq_int to return the filled INTSXP vector instead of NULL and stop leaking a protect stack entry; seq_int and asLogicalNoNA now use Sexp typed accessors/setters with focused tests. Release gate passed again: strict clippy, full tests, Android aarch64, 201/201 conformance, safe API audit, and git diff --check all green.
close_reason: Selected core modules now use safe helpers or strict denies, remaining legacy unsafe-op sites are scoped to measured module-level allows, and the full release gate is green.

title: Base parity: path helpers and sequence
description: Stock-R sweep found basename(), file.path(), and sequence() are missing or not routed from the evaluator. These are common script/package helpers and should have focused base-compatible implementations.
acceptance_criteria: basename('/tmp/foo.txt'), file.path('a','b','c.txt'), and sequence(c(2,3)) match stock R in conformance; Android temp/file helpers remain green.
close_reason: Implemented and routed sequence(), basename(), dirname(), and file.path(); added stock-R conformance cases 170-175; release gate passes with 179/179 conformance cases.

title: Base parity: environment named arguments and parent.env
description: Stock-R sweep found new.env(parent=emptyenv()), exists(..., envir=e), and with(data.frame(...), expr) fail with object 'Sexp(...)' lookup errors. Fix named environment arguments and evaluation in supplied environments.
acceptance_criteria: new.env(parent=emptyenv()) parent checks, exists(..., envir=e), and with(data.frame(...), a+b) match stock R in conformance.
close_reason: Implemented named environment arguments, parent.env parent matching, and with(data.frame(...), expr) evaluation; release gate passes.

title: Base parity: factor/table/as.character behavior
description: Stock-R sweep found as.character(factor(...)) returns the factor object/levels text instead of labels, and table(factor(...)) loses table names/formatting.
acceptance_criteria: as.character(factor(c('b','a','b'))) and table(factor(c('b','a','b'))) match stock R in conformance; existing factor labels case remains green.
close_reason: Implemented factor label coercion and table names/class printing; release gate passes.

title: Base parity: higher-order function calls
description: Stock-R sweep found apply(matrix(...), 1, sum), sapply(..., length), vapply(...), and do.call(sum, ...) fail because builtin/function values are evaluated or applied incorrectly in higher-order paths.
acceptance_criteria: apply row sum, sapply length, vapply length, and do.call(sum, list(...)) match stock R with conformance fixtures; closure and lapply regressions stay green.
close_reason: Implemented higher-order function parity for apply, sapply, vapply, and do.call; added stock-R conformance fixtures; release gate passes.

title: Base parity: matrix names and dimnames replacement
description: Stock-R sweep found dimnames<-(), rownames<-(), and colnames<-() on matrices fail through replacement evaluation. Implement the replacement path and preserve matrix print names.
acceptance_criteria: dimnames(m) <- list(...); m and rownames/colnames replacement cases match stock R in conformance; existing matrix dim/nrow/ncol cases remain green.
close_reason: Implemented matrix dimnames, rownames, and colnames replacement with stock-R print parity; added conformance fixtures; release gate passes.

title: Base parity: data.frame print and column subset
description: Stock-R sweep found data.frame() currently prints like a raw list and d['a'] loses data-frame formatting. Fix minimal data.frame class/row.names handling, print.data.frame dispatch, and one-column data-frame subset shape.
acceptance_criteria: data.frame(a=1:2,b=c('x','y')) and d <- data.frame(a=1:2,b=3:4); d['a'] match stock R output in conformance; existing list behavior remains green.
close_reason: Implemented data.frame print formatting and preserved data.frame shape for one-column subset; release gate passes.

title: Base parity: grep/grepl/sub/gsub argument matching
description: Stock-R sweep found grepl(), grep(value=TRUE), sub(), and gsub() either missing from dispatch or not matching common base semantics. Add focused conformance fixtures and route/fix the string matching helpers.
acceptance_criteria: grepl('a', c('cat','dog')), grep('a', ..., value=TRUE), sub(), and gsub() match stock R for fixed/simple regex cases; conformance cases are added; release gate passes.
close_reason: Implemented grep/grepl dispatch and common literal parity with conformance coverage; release gate passes.

title: Clippy zero-warning and unsafe-op cleanup
description: Make the workspace pass cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings without the release gate's temporary RUSTFLAGS=-Awarnings policy. Current failures include unresolved LAPACK backend import in stats/rwishart, 2024 unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn cleanup across legacy C-shaped modules, unused imports, mechanical clippy lints, and test should_panic expectations.
notes: 2026-04-25: strict clippy is now enforced by scripts/release_gate.sh by default. Added --no-strict-clippy only as a focused local-debugging escape hatch; release signoff should use the default strict path.
close_reason: Strict cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings now passes on stable and is enforced by the default release gate. Fixed hard blockers, converted the nightly-only bench to stable, documented source-faithful C-port lint policy, and filed rport-goz8 for the deeper unsafe-boundary reduction work.

title: Android security and sandbox policy
description: Define the runtime security model for Android: file access boundaries, temp/cache behavior, package library roots, system()/process behavior, native package policy, network assumptions, cancellation for runaway code, and resource limits. Users should know what embedded R can and cannot touch.
design: Prefer explicit Android path policy and clear errors over implicit host behavior. Do not silently grant broad filesystem or native-code access.
acceptance_criteria: Policy doc exists; runtime paths enforce app-private files/cache/library roots by default; tempdir and library paths are covered by tests; native-code policy is explicit; system()/process behavior is documented and constrained where possible; long-running eval can be cancelled; resource limit gaps are tracked.
notes: Builds on path policy, cancellation, and useDynLib rejection work.
close_reason: Documented Android sandbox/security policy, disabled system() on Android by runtime policy, linked policy docs, tracked remaining hard resource-limit gap as rport-wuoo, and passed full release gate.

title: Fuzzing and property tests for parser/eval/memory
description: Add adversarial confidence: fuzz parser inputs, malformed SEXP/accessor boundaries, vector indexing, package namespace parser, and selected evaluator paths. The goal is crash resistance and safe failure, especially for Android-hosted user input.
design: Use lightweight property tests in normal CI and longer fuzz targets as optional developer commands. Prioritize panic-free behavior and memory safety over exact semantic parity in fuzz mode.
acceptance_criteria: Fuzz/property tests exist for parser, namespace directive parser, vector/subset bounds, owned value conversion, and selected eval errors; fuzz corpus includes prior crashes; CI or local release gate documents how to run short and long fuzz modes; no fuzz target requires network or device.
notes: Paused by user preference: prioritize core safety/elegance/faithful Rust implementation work over adding more tests/fuzz harnesses right now.
close_reason: Added deterministic adversarial tests for parser, namespace parser, eval/subset errors, and owned value conversion; added short/long local script and docs; fixed a null-data read in c(...) by using checked element accessors; verified long adversarial mode, rmath lib tests, conformance, and clippy.

title: Upstream R sync and porting discipline
description: Document and enforce how Rust files map back to upstream R C/R sources so future R changes can be compared and reapplied. This preserves faithfulness while allowing Rust-shaped improvements.
design: Keep C-shaped structure where it helps diffing, but document Rust-shaped boundaries where exact structure would harm safety or Android embedding. Do not create brittle generated comments everywhere; focus on core files.
acceptance_criteria: Port map exists for major translated modules; each high-risk Rust module names upstream source/function anchors where practical; comparison workflow is documented; deviations from upstream behavior are tagged as Rust safety/design choices or known gaps; new conformance failures can be traced to source areas.
notes: Added checked upstream port map covering 81 source anchors across distributions, eval/parser, SEXP/session memory, mainutils, appl, graphics, and Android/UniFFI embedding. Wired scripts/check_upstream_port_map.sh into release_gate.sh and docs.
close_reason: Implemented checked upstream port map and release-gate enforcement. Verified scripts/check_upstream_port_map.sh, cargo fmt --check --all, git diff --check, and scripts/release_gate.sh --no-android --no-strict-clippy.

title: Performance benchmarks and memory profile
description: Measure and improve the runtime enough that it feels credible: startup, eval throughput, allocation pressure, package load time, plot rendering time, parallel session overhead, and Android target binary size. Reviewers should see evidence, not anecdotes.
design: Benchmark stable representative workloads, not microbenchmarks only. Keep release gate thresholds loose enough to avoid flaky CI but strong enough to catch accidental blowups.
acceptance_criteria: Criterion or equivalent benchmarks exist for core eval/vector/package/plot paths; memory allocation/arena stats are reported for representative scripts; Android binary/artifact size is measured; obvious regressions have thresholds; README/report includes benchmark snapshots and methodology.
notes: Added embedding performance probe, arena stats API, performance_report.sh, android_artifact_size.sh, docs/performance.md snapshot, and release docs. Verified quick performance thresholds plus Android release libr_uniffi.so size.
close_reason: Implemented representative performance/memory reporting with arena stats, thresholds, Android artifact size measurement, docs, and verified checks.

title: Package data lazyload and library ergonomics
description: Extend package support beyond code sourcing: data loading policy, lazy data where feasible, .libPaths/find.package/library/require edge cases, DESCRIPTION metadata fields, package attach/detach behavior, and namespace cache decisions. This makes the package story feel intentional.
design: Stay pure-R and Android-first. If full R lazyload is too much, define a minimal supported data format and clear rejection path for unsupported databases. Avoid process-global namespace caches unless they are per-session.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures cover data/ or R/sysdata-like package data where supported, .libPaths and find.package parity, repeated library/require calls, missing packages, native-code rejection, namespace imports, S3 registrations, and package metadata; unsupported lazyload/compiled features have explicit errors and beads.
notes: Additional package-runtime slice: installed.packages() now scans session library paths and returns an R-shaped character matrix with standard metadata columns and dim/dimnames; Android path test validates typed matrix shape. Full release gate passed again with 201/201 conformance and safe API audit clean. Remaining scope: data()/lazy data policy, detach/search-path edge cases, and package corpus smoke.
close_reason: Completed package runtime release slice: per-session namespace cache, rich package metadata, installed.packages matrix, pure-R data/*.R loading, explicit serialized/lazy/native data rejection, search/detach package ergonomics, Android package smoke, and full release gate with 201/201 conformance.

title: Stats RNG and numeric fidelity release slice
description: Harden the math/stats surface users hit early: distributions, RNG/session seeds, sample/sample.int, summary functions, NA/NaN/Inf handling, integer overflow, basic linear algebra where present, and tolerance-based comparison to stock R.
design: Use exact stock-R parity where deterministic and tolerance/invariant tests where exact streams or platform math differ. Prioritize APIs needed by package corpus and demo scripts.
acceptance_criteria: Conformance fixtures cover common distribution helpers with tail/log flags, RNG seed isolation, sample invariants, NA/NaN/Inf behavior, summary functions, and selected numerical edge cases; known stream incompatibilities are documented; Android tests cover the public eval surface; failures create child beads.
notes: Builds on rport-pm0 and rport-1pm.
close_reason: Hardened stats/RNG conformance slice. sample() now handles R's numeric shortcut, named arguments, typed vector sampling, names preservation, replacement constraints, and weighted probability sampling. Added Android eval coverage plus stock-R conformance fixtures for sample behavior, distribution tail/log flags, numeric edge predicates, and probability-sampling errors. Documented RNG stream policy. Verified with scripts/release_gate.sh --android-package (206/206 conformance).

title: Graphics path release quality
description: Make plotting good enough for Android demos and credible enough for reviewers. Improve the current r-embed/headless path while tracking the longer-term rmath graphics-engine route. Cover common plot arguments, text, axes, dimensions, error handling, and visual regression tests.
design: For shippability, improve the current Android renderer first. Do not block release on a full R graphics engine unless package corpus requires it. Keep visual tests deterministic and pixel-region based, not brittle exact screenshots.
acceptance_criteria: Render tests decode PNGs and verify nonblank plot, labels, axes, colors, point/line modes, Unicode labels, small/large dimensions, and invalid inputs; UniFFI render returns actionable errors; demo includes at least two useful plots; remaining full graphics-engine gaps are tracked separately.
notes: Builds on fed1ad6 and rport-z8d.
close_reason: Improved the shippable Android headless renderer path: direct r-embed dimension validation, UniFFI minimum-size validation, lwd/cex plot option support, point radius rendering, PNG pixel tests for point mode and small/large canvases, actionable render-error tests, updated Android embedding docs with two demo plots, and recorded deeper graphics-device gaps on rport-z8d. Verified with scripts/release_gate.sh --android-package (206/206 conformance).

title: Object system S3 release parity
description: Move S3 from first working slice to release-grade parity for common packages: UseMethod, NextMethod, getS3method/hasS3method, registered namespace methods, replacement methods, group generics where feasible, class vectors, and method lookup order.
design: Keep the C structure in mainutils::objects recognizable, but remove ad hoc duplicate dispatch paths when possible. Prefer one lookup helper used by direct generic calls, UseMethod, getS3method, and namespace registration.
acceptance_criteria: Stock-R fixtures cover UseMethod direct dispatch, hidden namespace methods, explicit registerS3method, S3method with custom method name, NextMethod simple inheritance, default methods, multiple classes, and missing method errors; package corpus exercises at least one real S3-heavy pure-R package or fixture; known gaps such as full base namespace distinction are documented or fixed.
notes:
Builds on commit e288d3a. Links to rport-fs5.
Thread-safety proof found that package S3 dispatch works for classed integer objects but fails for a package-created list object with object 'Sexp(1, len=0)' not found. Keep list/data-frame S3 dispatch in this release parity slice.
close_reason: Centralized S3 method lookup in objects.rs; direct generic dispatch, UseMethod, getS3method/hasS3method/register helpers now share the lookup path; release gate passed.

title: Unsafe/raw SEXP public boundary audit
description: Make unsafe/raw SEXP entrypoints private or explicitly unsafe where possible, preserve internal C-shaped ABI where needed, and ensure safe public APIs return lifetime-bound Sexp or owned values.
notes: Next slice: typed Environment facade to retire raw env ergonomics from session/eval safe paths.
close_reason: Closed as completed by the release-readiness milestone: current full gate passes, conformance is 206/206, app-facing APIs are safe/owned, multi-instance Android/UniFFI/package/graphics flows are tested and documented, and remaining known limits are captured in release docs.

title: SEXP object model module split
description: Split sexp::object into smaller Rust-shaped modules: error/result types, borrowed Sexp access, owned SexpValue projection, metadata extraction, SexpView, and pairlist iteration. Keep public rmath::sexp re-exports stable and avoid behavior changes.
close_reason: Split sexp::object into focused error, value, view, owned projection, pairlist, and core Sexp modules while preserving public re-exports and passing full Rust/Android gates.

title: Evaluator Rust-shaped boundary cleanup
description: Reduce raw SEXP plumbing in eval.rs and adjacent evaluator modules by introducing owner-scoped helper APIs where practical, keeping C structure recognizable and preserving behavior.
notes: Evaluator visibility control now includes library(), preserving the primitive's explicit invisible return instead of resetting visibility after builtin dispatch.
close_reason: Closed as completed by the release-readiness milestone: current full gate passes, conformance is 206/206, app-facing APIs are safe/owned, multi-instance Android/UniFFI/package/graphics flows are tested and documented, and remaining known limits are captured in release docs.

title: Multi-instance global state audit and fixes
description: Identify and remove remaining process-global or thread-local state that prevents clean parallel R sessions. Move mutable runtime state into RInstance where feasible, keep immutable sentinels explicit, and update Android global checks.
notes: Removed the remaining process-global environment fallback from sexp::globals/init: R_GlobalEnv/R_BaseEnv/R_EmptyEnv now require an active RInstance and set_* mutates the active instance. initialize_r/shutdown_r no longer carry AtomicBool/Mutex process startup state; RInstance initializes base bindings during construction. Removed stale sexp/init.rs allowlist entry and updated globals.rs policy note. Gates passed: full rmath lib tests, r-embed/r-uniffi tests, Android aarch64 check, Android globals scan, diff check.
close_reason: Closed as completed by the release-readiness milestone: current full gate passes, conformance is 206/206, app-facing APIs are safe/owned, multi-instance Android/UniFFI/package/graphics flows are tested and documented, and remaining known limits are captured in release docs.

title: Android runtime product surface milestone
description: Define and implement the first Android-ready runtime surface beyond the core: safe UniFFI session API, package/library hooks, graphics/output boundaries, and multi-tab session behavior.
close_reason: Exposed Android runtime path/session info through rmath, r-embed, and UniFFI; verified Android target and global allowlist.

title: Reduce raw SEXP plumbing in evaluator
description: Harden evaluator entry points around typed wrappers/results and reduce direct raw SEXP manipulation in eval, assignment, missing, and parser handoffs.
close_reason: Moved Android parse/eval onto session-owned eval_code_with_output_capture, keeping parsing and evaluation behind owner-checked Sexp boundaries.

title: Use checked atomic element formatting
description: Why: sexp::output still formats integer, real, and logical elements with unwrap_or fallbacks that can hide malformed vectors as zero, NA, or NaN. What: centralize atomic element formatting through checked Sexp accessors and use it in scalar, vector, and matrix output paths.
close_reason: Replaced atomic output fallbacks with checked Sexp element formatting and tests for visible access errors.

title: Use safe CHARSXP formatting in output
description: Why: sexp::output still formats STRSXP by calling raw CHAR/CStr and falling back to empty strings, duplicating safe Sexp string access and losing NA_character_ fidelity. What: centralize string element formatting on Sexp::try_string_elt/try_as_str, render NA explicitly, and remove raw CHAR usage from output formatting.
close_reason: Replaced raw CHAR/CStr string output formatting with checked Sexp accessors and explicit NA rendering.

title: Preserve NA strings in owned SEXP values
description: Why: Android and UniFFI typed values still flatten NA_character_ to an empty string, which is a lossy fallback and less idiomatic than Option<String>. What: carry string vectors as Vec<Option<String>> through rmath Android values, r-embed, and UniFFI, and update tests so missing strings remain explicit.
close_reason: Preserved NA_character_ as None through Android, r-embed, and UniFFI typed values.

title: Add owned Rust SEXP projection for UniFFI boundaries
description: Why: Sexp is safer now, but embedding and UniFFI-facing code still need a pure Rust value shape instead of reaching for raw SEXP pointers or borrowed C-shaped slices. What: add an owned SexpValue projection with checked conversion from Sexp, covering common scalar/vector/list/string/nil/function/object shapes without changing runtime representation.
close_reason: Added owned SexpValue projection, Android adapter conversion, UniFFI raw/complex value support, and tests.

title: Migrate mainutils pairlist handling to checked SEXP APIs
description: Why: runtime helper modules still parse R argument pairlists with legacy Option car/cdr/tag accessors, which silently turn malformed structures into default behavior. What: migrate coercion, character, and unique argument handling to typed try_* APIs while preserving existing FFI fallback semantics at public entry points.
close_reason: Added checked pairlist argument helpers to Sexp and migrated mainutils character/coerce/unique argument handling to them; validation passed.

title: Move native package registries into session-aware runtime
description: mainutils/rdynload.rs, dotcode.rs, connections.rs, dynload.rs, and symbol/native registration paths still use AtomicPtr/AtomicUsize/Mutex/TLS registries. Android package loading needs an explicit per-session or shared-immutable policy.
acceptance_criteria: Native symbol, DLL, connection, and .C/.Call option registries have a documented session/shared boundary; Android RSession tests cover independent registry-visible state where mutable.
notes: Completed unix dynload slice: removed thread-local mutable OS dynamic symbol vtable. The vtable is now immutable fixed platform function pointers computed on demand, while InitFunctionHashing remains a compatibility no-op/validation entrypoint. unix::dynload, rdynload, connections, and android focused tests pass.
close_reason: Native package registry scope completed: dotcode symbol caches are session-local/immutable, rdynload DLL and C-callable registries are RSession-owned, connections/sink state is RSession-owned, and unix dynload vtable is immutable. Focused native registry, session, and Android tests pass.

title: Move graphics and device registries into Android session state
description: graphics/grDevices/grid modules still have TLS and OnceLock<Mutex> registries for device state, palettes, font caches, graphics engine counts, and plot scratch buffers. Android graphics bridge needs explicit session/device ownership.
acceptance_criteria: Android graphics device bridge owns device registry/palette/graphics parameters per session or per device; desktop-only caches are allowlisted; tests cover two sessions with independent active devices.
notes: Completed session-state slices: graphics device registry, graphics engine count, grDevices palette, grid runtime/eval state, plot3d scratch state, graphics::plot dendrogram scratch state, grDevices PostScript/PDF font registries, and grDevices Windows backend scratch/font placeholders. Remaining graphics TLS audit: graphics/xspline.rs TLS appears orphaned/not wired into graphics::mod.rs; device_registry TEST_LOCK is test-only. Focused grDevices/graphics/grid/android tests pass.
close_reason: Moved compiled graphics/grDevices/grid mutable registries and scratch state into RSession: device registry, engine count, palette, grid runtime/eval state, plot3d, dendrogram, PostScript/PDF font registries, and Windows backend placeholders. Remaining xspline TLS is in an orphan source file not wired into graphics::mod.rs; device_registry Mutex is test-only. Focused graphics, grDevices, grid, and Android session tests pass.

title: Define Android platform global allowlist
description: Unix/X11/TclTk/internet/intl/timezone/graphapp translated globals are not all part of the initial Android embedding path, but must be explicitly allowlisted, disabled, or replaced to avoid accidental linkage of non-session state.
acceptance_criteria: A checked Android allowlist documents immutable shared data, session fallbacks, disabled desktop modules, and platform replacements; Android build excludes or gates unsupported mutable globals.
notes: Moved mainutils::memory_main GC control counters and pending C finalizer queue into RInstance memory_state; removed thread-local runtime state and allowlist row. Gates: memory_main tests 20/20, android tests 67/67, conformance 164/164, Android target check, global scan, diff check.
close_reason: Added checked Android mutable-global allowlist and wired it into android_toolchain_check; gated unsupported desktop/platform modules from Android target while preserving unix::dynload. Android toolchain check passes.

title: Move error warning interrupt state into RInstance
description: mainutils/errors.rs still uses AtomicI32/AtomicBool/AtomicPtr for IN_ERROR, warning collection, interrupt pending/suspended, R_Expressions, and warning buffers. These must be session-owned for parallel Android sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Errors, warnings, interrupts, and expression limits are scoped to active RSession with fallback for non-session callers; tests cover two sessions triggering independent warnings/errors.
close_reason: Error/warning/interrupt/expression state plus condition handler and restart stacks now route through active RInstance with fallback atomics/TLS for non-session callers; added same-thread RSession isolation tests.

title: Move evaluator control state into RInstance
description: Evaluator limits, visibility/depth, bytecode stack, JIT flags, profiling state, and missing-argument interpreter flags still use TLS/global state in eval/*, sexp/globals.rs, and mainutils/main.rs. Move Android RSession execution paths to instance-owned state with compatibility fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Two RSession instances keep eval depth, visibility, JIT/profiling toggles, and bytecode stack state isolated; focused eval/session tests pass.
notes: Completed profiling slice: Rprof flags, profiler output/source buffers, profiling event, bytecode profiling flag/current opcode/opcode counts, and srcref now live in RInstance.eval_state.profiling with required active-instance access and no mutable fallback. Added same-thread two-session profiling isolation tests; focused eval/main/errors/session/android suites pass.
close_reason: Evaluator control state moved into RInstance: main/eval flags, bytecode/JIT/missing state, and profiling state are session-owned and covered by same-thread RSession isolation tests.

title: Move environment and allocation side tables into RInstance
description: sexp/env_hash.rs and sexp/memory_ext.rs keep environment hash tables, raw cons tracking, and VMAX allocations in TLS. They are runtime-owned tables and should follow RInstance on the Android/session path.
acceptance_criteria: Env hash tables, raw cons state, and VMAX allocations route through active RInstance; compatibility fallback remains; two-session tests cover independent env/hash allocation behavior.
close_reason: Environment hash tables, raw cons tracking, and VMAX transient allocations now route through active RInstance with TLS fallback; added same-thread RSession isolation tests.

title: Move R RNG kind and sampler caches into RInstance
description: Core rng/base.rs is session-local, but mainutils/rng.rs, mainutils/rng_dispatch.rs, dist/* and nmath/dist/* still have global/TLS RNG kind and distribution sampler caches. Android sessions need these scoped or made pure.
acceptance_criteria: RNG kind, .Random.seed-facing state, and cached samplers for binomial/poisson/gamma/beta/hypergeometric/signrank/wilcox are isolated per RSession; math/RNG tests cover two sessions.
notes: Completed final slice: beta sampler caches in dist/ and nmath/dist/ now live in RInstance with required active-instance access, and rng/base.rs no longer has a TLS fallback. Audit leaves only immutable lookup/builtin initialization (exponential Q table and RNG_SEXPS OnceLock). rbeta_state, mainutils::random, rng_dispatch, android, and session focused tests pass.
close_reason: RNG kind/state and distribution sampler caches are session-owned: mainutils RNG state, nmath RNG facade, rank/binomial/poisson/hypergeometric/gamma/beta caches moved to RInstance with isolation tests; rng/base fallback TLS removed.

title: Packages and namespace loading conformance
description: Implement/validate library(), require(), namespace loading, DESCRIPTION/NAMESPACE parsing, lazy data, compiled code policy, and package search paths.
acceptance_criteria: A minimal pure-R package can load and run tests; unsupported native package behavior is explicitly tracked.
notes: Added explicit pure-R Android package policy for NAMESPACE useDynLib(...): native-code packages now fail package load with a clear error before partial attach instead of silently ignoring native requirements. Regression covers useDynLib(tiny). Gates: full rmath --lib, Android aarch64 check, globals scan, diff check.
close_reason: Closed as completed by the release-readiness milestone: current full gate passes, conformance is 206/206, app-facing APIs are safe/owned, multi-instance Android/UniFFI/package/graphics flows are tested and documented, and remaining known limits are captured in release docs.

title: Stats and math conformance sweep
description: Validate distributions, RNG, model helpers, linear algebra, complex arithmetic, optim/polyroot/fft where present, and numerical edge cases.
acceptance_criteria: Stock-R numeric goldens with tolerances exist; Android-safe native dependencies are identified.
notes: Exposed sample.int for uniform integer sampling with replace TRUE/FALSE, duplicate-free without-replacement selection, and R-like size > n error. Tests use invariant parity rather than exact RNG stream parity because current RNG seed stream is not GNU R-compatible.
close_reason: Closed as completed by the release-readiness milestone: current full gate passes, conformance is 206/206, app-facing APIs are safe/owned, multi-instance Android/UniFFI/package/graphics flows are tested and documented, and remaining known limits are captured in release docs.

title: Base functions conformance sweep
description: Compare base functions needed for scripts/packages: apply/lapply, environments, match/unique/order/sort, strings/grep, dates, serialize, connections, errors/warnings.
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs categories against stock R and Rust runtime; mismatches are fixed or filed.
notes: Corrected system() semantics: registered public function, default path captures child stdout/stderr and returns invisible exit status, intern=TRUE returns stdout lines as STRSXP.
close_reason: Closed as completed by the release-readiness milestone: current full gate passes, conformance is 206/206, app-facing APIs are safe/owned, multi-instance Android/UniFFI/package/graphics flows are tested and documented, and remaining known limits are captured in release docs.

title: Object system conformance
description: Validate S3/S4 method dispatch, class attributes, UseMethod/NextMethod, group generics, replacement functions, and namespace lookup.
acceptance_criteria: Representative S3 and S4 golden tests pass or blocked gaps are tracked.
notes: Implemented a real first S3 registry slice: getS3method/hasS3method/registerS3method now use .__S3MethodsTable__.; NAMESPACE S3method(generic, class[, method]) registers package-private methods; UseMethod is routed to mainutils::objects and closure evaluation now preserves the real call expression needed by S3 dispatch. Regression loads a pure-R package with hidden tiny_generic.myclass and dispatches tiny_generic(structure-like class assignment) through UseMethod. Gates: full rmath --lib, r-embed/r-uniffi tests, Android aarch64 check, globals scan, diff check.
close_reason: Closed as completed by the release-readiness milestone: current full gate passes, conformance is 206/206, app-facing APIs are safe/owned, multi-instance Android/UniFFI/package/graphics flows are tested and documented, and remaining known limits are captured in release docs.

title: Android graphics device bridge
description: Implement a graphics-device bridge for Android rendering: capture plots to bitmap/vector commands and expose them through the embedding API.
acceptance_criteria: Basic plot produces a renderable Android-facing artifact; device state is per session.
notes: Implemented Android-facing basic plot render bridge: r-embed render_with_dimensions now evaluates simple numeric plot expressions on the owning session, renders axes/points/lines through AndroidHeadlessRenderer, and returns PNG bytes. UniFFI render now passes plot code to the worker-owned session. Validation: cargo test -p r-embed -p r-uniffi -- --test-threads=1; cargo check -p rmath -p r-embed -p r-uniffi; cargo check --target aarch64-linux-android -p r-embed -p r-uniffi; scripts/check_android_globals.sh; git diff --check.
close_reason: Basic Android plot rendering now returns PNG bytes from session-evaluated numeric plot data via r-embed and UniFFI.

title: Android interrupt/cancellation support
description: RStudio-like Android needs cancelling long evals. Add cooperative cancellation checks wired to session state instead of process-global flags.
acceptance_criteria: Long-running eval can be cancelled per session; cancellation does not poison other sessions.
notes: Implementing session-local cooperative cancellation for Android embedding: per-eval cancellation token is stored on RInstance eval_state, checked by evaluator/loop paths, and exposed through r-embed without raw SEXP. Adding isolation regression before closing.
close_reason: Implemented session-local cooperative cancellation: RInstance eval_state holds an explicit cancellation token, Rf_eval and special-form loops check it, r-embed exposes a safe CancellationToken API, UniFFI cancel flips the active token directly, and regressions cover running cancellation plus no poisoning of idle/other sessions. Gates passed: r-embed tests, r-uniffi tests, rmath Android tests, Android aarch64 check, conformance 39/39, Android globals scan, git diff --check.

title: Android package/library path policy
description: Define how .libPaths(), user library, bundled base/recommended packages, cache dirs, temp dirs, and permissions work on Android.
acceptance_criteria: Policy is implemented or documented with tests for path resolution; no hardcoded desktop paths on Android.
notes: Implemented per-instance RuntimePathPolicy for library/temp/cache paths; .libPaths(), find.package(), library(), require(), tempdir(), and tempfile() now resolve through session state. Added Android/r-embed/UniFFI configure_android_paths hooks and tests proving app-private library/temp paths and package lookup. Validation: cargo check -p rmath -p r-embed -p r-uniffi; cargo test -p rmath --lib -- --test-threads=1; cargo test -p r-embed -p r-uniffi -- --test-threads=1; cargo test -p rmath --doc; scripts/conformance_parity.sh; cargo check --target aarch64-linux-android -p rmath -p r-embed -p r-uniffi; scripts/check_android_globals.sh; git diff --check.
close_reason: Per-session Android path policy is implemented, exposed through embedding APIs, tested, and validated.

title: Design UniFFI-safe Android API handles
description: Expose sessions, values, output events, errors, and plot handles using owned Rust types and opaque IDs suitable for Kotlin/Java.
acceptance_criteria: No raw SEXP crosses FFI; API supports eval, inspect value, get output, close session; UniFFI scaffolding compiles or is documented.
notes: Completed typed UniFFI eval result export: added RValueKind/RValue records, EvalResult now carries output plus owned value, callbacks receive the typed EvalResult, eval() remains string compatibility, and eval_result() exposes inspectable values to Kotlin/Java. Gates: cargo test -p r-uniffi passed; aarch64-linux-android cargo check -p r-uniffi passed; git diff --check passed.
close_reason: Owned Android/UniFFI API boundary is in place: r-embed and UniFFI expose sessions, output, typed values, errors, plots, close/cancel without raw SEXP crossing the boundary; UniFFI scaffolding and Android target checks pass.

title: Move output capture into RSession
description: Output capture currently uses thread-local mutex-backed strings. Android needs per-session stdout/stderr capture and streaming hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Session eval returns/captures output independently; two sessions on parallel threads do not mix output.
close_reason: Fixed for session path: capture buffers now live in RInstance when active, with TLS fallback for legacy calls; added scoped RSession capture helper and isolation test.

title: Audit all mutable globals/TLS for Android session safety
description: Catalog every Atomic/Mutex/OnceLock/thread_local/static mutable runtime state and classify it as immutable runtime data, session state, compatibility fallback, or unsafe blocker.
acceptance_criteria: Audit artifact exists in beads notes or docs; blockers have follow-up beads; Android path has an explicit allowlist.
notes: Audit summary (2026-04-24): Android RSession path now has instance-owned arena/env/protect/preserve/symbol/RNG/output/context/GC state. Allowed shared/compatibility state: immutable sentinel SEXPs and constants in sexp/globals.rs, per-session dispatch pointer CURRENT_INSTANCE, and legacy fallback TLS/Mutex/OnceLock used only when no RSession is active. Remaining blockers filed from this audit: rport-86r.1 error/warning/interrupt state; rport-86r.2 evaluator visibility/depth/JIT/profiling/bytecode state; rport-86r.3 env_hash/raw-cons/VMAX side tables; rport-86r.4 R RNG kind and distribution sampler caches; rport-86r.5 native/package registries; rport-dg0.1 graphics/device registries; rport-dg0.2 Android platform allowlist. Desktop/platform modules with TLS (unix, X11, TclTk, graphapp, internet, intl/timezone) are not acceptable by default for Android linkage and must be allowlisted, disabled, or replaced under rport-dg0.2.
close_reason: Cataloged mutable globals/TLS, documented Android/session allowlist in notes, and filed follow-up blocker beads for remaining unsafe runtime/platform state.

title: Move RNG state into RInstance
description: RNG state is thread-local/global today. R sessions need independent RNG streams for parallel Android notebooks and reproducibility.
acceptance_criteria: set.seed-like behavior is session-local; two sessions do not advance each other's RNG; distribution tests pass.
close_reason: Fixed for session/Android path: RNG seed state now lives in RInstance when active, with thread-local fallback for non-session code; Android exposes set_seed and tests same-thread isolation.

title: Move GC state into RInstance
description: GC stats, callbacks, card tables, remembered sets, and in-progress flags are thread-local today. Instance-owned GC state is required for independent sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Minor GC uses session-owned state on the RSession path; two sessions can GC independently; existing GC tests pass.
close_reason: GC stats, callbacks, in-progress flag, card table, and remembered set now live in active RInstance with fallback state; added same-thread RSession GC isolation tests.

title: Move protect and preserve stacks into RInstance
description: Protection stacks are partially instance-aware but still have thread-local fallbacks. Complete the session-owned path and test isolation.
acceptance_criteria: Session eval/protect uses instance-owned stacks; fallback stacks are compatibility-only; parallel sessions do not share protection depth.
close_reason: Fixed: preserve stack now routes through RInstance like protect stack, with TLS fallback for legacy code; added same-thread two-session protect/preserve isolation test.

title: Move context stack into RInstance
description: The R context stack is thread-local today. Move or route it through RInstance for clean session isolation and parallel execution.
acceptance_criteria: Context operations use current/explicit instance state for session eval; tests cover two sessions with independent return/error contexts.
close_reason: Context stack and in-error state now route through active RInstance with legacy fallback; added same-thread RSession isolation tests.

title: Only clear RSession thread-local instance when it owns it
description: RSession::new can replace the thread-local current RInstance, but close/drop currently call clear_current_instance unconditionally. Closing or dropping an older non-current session can clear a newer active session on the same thread. Add pointer-checked clearing and regression tests.
close_reason: Fixed: added pointer-checked thread-local clearing and covered close/drop of non-current sessions.

title: Make RSession symbol interning safe for Rust strings
description: RSession::find_var and define_var currently pass name.as_ptr() directly to Rf_install, but Rust &str is not NUL-terminated. This can read past the string buffer and makes the embedding API unsound. Convert these paths to checked CString construction and add regression tests for ordinary and interior-NUL names.
close_reason: Fixed: RSession now interns Rust strings through CString, rejects interior NUL names, and sexp::session is compiled/tested.

title: Define Rust R port architecture map and upstream sync strategy
description: Document the layered architecture for the C-to-Rust R port: raw repr(C) compatibility layer, safe SEXP handles, evaluator/runtime ownership, Android embedding surface, and rules for when to stay structurally close to upstream R versus using Rust-native abstractions. Include a rebase/import workflow so future R upstream changes can be reapplied without losing Rust-specific safety work.
notes: Added docs/rust-r-port-architecture.md covering raw compatibility layer, RInstance/RArena/Sexp ownership, Rust-shaped evaluator entrypoints, Android embedding boundaries, upstream sync workflow, and conformance gates.
close_reason: Architecture and upstream sync strategy documented in docs/rust-r-port-architecture.md.

title: Build Android-first conformance milestone for embedded R runtime
description: Create a concrete Android milestone for the RStudio-like goal: headless evaluation API, output capture, package/library path policy, pure-Rust native dependencies, graphics-device bridge, and conformance cases that run against both stock R and the Android-capable Rust runtime.
notes: Finished broad test-suite ownership cleanup after removing ambient allocation fallback: full rmath --lib now passes sequentially with 1860 passed, 4 ignored, 0 failed. Converted remaining mainutils/grid/sexp/unix raw-allocation tests to create explicit RSession owners; parser tests avoid mutable globals while keeping parse-tree sessions alive. Gates: full rmath --lib --test-threads=1, conformance 164/164, rmath/r-embed/r-uniffi cargo check, Android aarch64 cargo check, Android globals scan, diff check, rustfmt check.
close_reason: Closed as completed by the release-readiness milestone: current full gate passes, conformance is 206/206, app-facing APIs are safe/owned, multi-instance Android/UniFFI/package/graphics flows are tested and documented, and remaining known limits are captured in release docs.

title: Harden SEXP safe wrapper for faithful Rust runtime
description: The Rust R port needs a SEXP abstraction that remains close to R's raw SEXPREC layout for future upstream diffing while exposing safer, typed, idiomatic Rust APIs. This session will audit the current Sexp wrapper, tighten type-correct access, and document follow-up architecture for Android/mobile runtime work.
notes: Found and fixed an important SEXP safety issue: atomic accessors and slice/iterator APIs were only checking generic vector-ness, so wrong typed reads such as integer_elt on REALSXP could reinterpret memory. Current patch makes safe.rs exact-type checked while preserving raw SEXPREC layout.
close_reason: Tightened SEXP safe wrapper type checks, made typed slice/iterator APIs safe, fixed logical output to use logical iteration, and added regression tests.

title: Integrate src/library subtree into active rmath crate
description: Why: the remaining grid and grDevices parity work now depends on wiring rmath/src/library into the active crate module graph. title: SEXP free_node can be revisited by GC and double-free payload
description:
Why: memory.rs free_node deallocates payload and pushes node onto free_list, but arena.nodes() still iterates those nodes and later GC passes can revisit/free stale payload state. This risks double-free/use-after-free behavior in GC paths.

What: ensure freed nodes are excluded from GC scans or have their payload/generation/mark state cleared so repeated reclamation is impossible. Add a regression test that frees and then runs repeated GC cycles.

Done: repeated GC cycles do not attempt to reclaim already-freed node payloads; regression test passes.
notes: Implemented in commit 8488b55. RArena::free_node is now idempotent (returns early if pointer already in free_list), and freed nodes are tombstoned: gengc_next_node cleared, attrib cleared, mark cleared, and generation set to Old to avoid repeated young-collection free attempts. Added regression coverage: sexp::memory::tests::test_arena_free_node_idempotent, test_arena_free_vector_clears_payload_pointer, and sexp::gengc::tests::test_minor_gc_does_not_refree_nodes_on_free_list. Validation: cargo test -p rmath sexp::memory::tests::test_arena_free_node_idempotent -- --exact; cargo test -p rmath sexp::memory::tests::test_arena_free_vector_clears_payload_pointer -- --exact; cargo test -p rmath sexp::gengc::tests::test_minor_gc_does_not_refree_nodes_on_free_list -- --exact.
close_reason: Closed

title: SEXP GC compaction treats atomic vectors as SEXP pointers
description:
Why: full GC compaction in gengc.rs currently casts vector payloads to SEXP* for all vector SEXPTYPEs. This is only valid for pointer vectors (VECSXP/EXPRSXP/STRSXP), but is UB for atomic vectors (INTSXP/REALSXP/LGLSXP/CPLXSXP/RAWSXP) and can corrupt memory during reference updates.

What: split compaction/update logic by payload kind and only walk pointer-bearing vectors as SEXP references. Atomic vectors should be copied/compacted as opaque bytes without per-element pointer rewriting. Add regression tests that compact each vector kind.

Done: compaction no longer reinterprets atomic payloads as SEXP pointers; tests cover vector-type-specific compaction behavior and pass.
notes: Implemented in commit 09576fa. GC reference-rewrite phases in sexp/gengc.rs now only walk pointer-bearing vector payloads (STRSXP/VECSXP/EXPRSXP) via vector_payload_has_sexp_refs(), instead of all is_vector_type() payloads. This removes UB reinterpretation of atomic payloads as SEXP*. Added regression tests: test_update_object_references_skips_atomic_vector_payloads (REALSXP payload bit-pattern remains unchanged even when matching a mapped old pointer) and test_update_object_references_updates_pointer_vector_payloads (VECSXP payload is correctly rewritten). Validation: cargo test -p rmath sexp::gengc::tests::test_update_object_references_skips_atomic_vector_payloads -- --exact; cargo test -p rmath sexp::gengc::tests::test_update_object_references_updates_pointer_vector_payloads -- --exact.
close_reason: Closed

title: try() try-error strings differ when stop(call.=FALSE)
description:
classes-methods.R:272 identical(err1, err1Y) for BaseGeneric(1) vs BaseGeneric(1, Y=2).

GNU stop(..., call.=FALSE) + try() yields identical try-errors because conditionCall is empty and the printed prefix is 'Error : '.

rport do_try always deparses the tried expression into 'Error in <expr> :', so the character payloads differ. condition$call is also doTryCatch(...), not NULL.

do_try should use conditionCall(e) (empty when errorcall(R_NilValue)) like GNU New-Internal.R.
notes: Threading call-less from verrorcall_dflt into do_try so GNU Error : prefix and NULL conditionCall apply to every errorcall(R_NilValue) site, not just BaseGeneric.
close_reason: try() now uses Error : and a NULL condition call when verrorcall_dflt saw an empty call. classes-methods.R identical(err1, err1Y) is pinned.

title: Protection stack APIs fail open on allocation failure
description:
Why: protect.rs currently swallows try_reserve failures in Rf_protect/R_ProtectWithIndex/R_PreserveObject. Calls appear successful even when values were not protected, creating latent GC safety bugs.

What: make protection APIs fail closed (explicit error or status) when stack growth fails, and align index-return behavior so callers cannot receive a bogus sentinel that looks valid. Add tests for simulated allocation failure paths.

Done: failed protection allocation is surfaced explicitly and never reports success; tests cover failure semantics.
notes: Implemented fail-closed semantics for protection stack allocation in commit 0cdbebd. Rf_protect, R_ProtectWithIndex, and R_PreserveObject now route through reserve_slot_or_fail and panic on reserve failure instead of silently succeeding. Added test-only reserve-failure hook plus regression tests: sexp::protect::tests::test_protect_reserve_failure_panics, test_protect_with_index_reserve_failure_panics, and test_preserve_reserve_failure_panics. Also corrected protect_n documentation to reflect actual RAII semantics (unprotect guard over pre-protected entries).
close_reason: Closed

notes:
Parity audit 2026-04-16: confirmed real behavioral gaps remain in grid.rs for doSetViewport, L_setviewport, L_downviewport, and L_downvppath. Specifically: doSetViewport still lacks parent-child registration and the clip/mask establishment branches; L_setviewport still lacks fill resolution plus clip-path/mask resolution; L_downviewport still lacks not-found error behavior and clip/mask restoration; L_downvppath still ignores its path argument and currently uses the plain viewport search helper. These are runtime bugs, not cosmetic drift.
Closed children rport-49p.2 and rport-49p.3 via bea2f95 (clip establishment + release hooks). Opened follow-up rport-49p.4 for real remaining parity gap: L_downvppath path argument semantics and down-navigation miss-error behavior.
Closed rport-49p.4 via e2ee78e (path-aware downvppath + miss-error parity).
close_reason: Core viewport/layout/unit parity gaps targeted by this bead are now implemented via commits b338bf9, bea2f95, and e2ee78e (pop/unset, clip establishment/release hooks, downvppath path+miss-error semantics). Remaining broader grid TODO comments are outside this bead’s scoped runtime regressions and can be tracked separately if promoted.
